items.title: A coding agent arriving at this repository has no front door, and the obvious fix would copy the tables the gate already checks
items.why: Five entry points that Claude Code and Codex look for by name are absent: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .codex, .github/copilot-instructions.md, and any committed .claude content - the only .claude file present is settings.local.json, which a global ignore keeps out of git. So every session rediscovers the bands, the ledger verbs, the gate and the traps from source, and the traps are the half written down nowhere: cargo fmt damages the tree, a stale copied nomos.exe silently strips ledger fields it does not know, work finish runs the gate lint step before the predicate, and the ledger is shared with other live sessions. That would have been the defect rather than the fix: the README band tables are compared against the workspace in both directions by tests/contract/tests/boundaries.rs, so a second copy is an unchecked copy, and OD-PROJECT-001 already settled that this repository does not keep two documents answering one question.

items.title: A repository can declare a projection mandatory, and a missing one fails closed
items.why: nomos spec freshness answers "what governed outputs are present here, and are the ones I found fresh?". A gate needs the other question: "are all outputs this repository declares mandatory present and fresh?". Measured on a corpus-less shell: freshness over an empty build root prints "checked 0 of 14" and exits 0, and deleting both halves of a governed output moves it to "not built here" and still exits 0. The half-present pairs and the edited body are already caught and tested at exit 8, so the hole is not the comparison - it is that nothing declares which outputs must exist. Requiredness is a property of this repository, not of a projection, so it does not belong on Profile beside format and output. It also cannot be derived from the directory being checked, which is OD-SPEC-005 refusing to compare a directory against itself.
items.done_when: freshness takes a repeatable --require <profile-id>. A required profile whose output and sidecar are both absent fails, as do output-without-sidecar, sidecar-without-output, an edited body and a stamp whose recorded inputs no longer match the store. An optional profile absent from the build root stays "not built here" and stays green, so a scratch root holding a subset is unaffected. An unknown --require id is a refusal that names the profiles that exist, not a missing output. Absent-because-the-corpus-is-unreadable stays its own answer and is not bent into staleness. diagrams/relations.mmd and its sidecar are committed, and the gate runs freshness --require diagram-set over the tree, which is green on a runner holding no corpus because that profile reads only the embedded governing records.

items.title: Nomos, KWB, XVPE and repository tooling have no recorded ownership boundary, and the only thing written down about the seam is a dependency rule
items.why: Four products share one design conversation and nothing in this repository records where one ends and the next begins. XVPE appears here as a style sibling and in D-130, which decides that no crate depends on it before Phase 5 and never by path - a dependency rule rather than an ownership rule. KWB appears five times, all incidental. So the seam that decides whether a subsystem belongs to knowledge, to generic runtime, to software engineering reality, or to the machinery that only exists to build this repository, is currently held in conversation and in nobody file. OD-AGENT-001 refused to write it into AGENTS.md, correctly: an instruction file nobody reviews would have promoted a design discussion into normative architecture. That refusal left a clean placeholder saying the question is unresolved, and this item is the answer going where an answer belongs. It is worth doing before more work accumulates across the seam, because every subsystem placed without it is a placement that later has to be argued about rather than read.
items.done_when: A canonical record states what each of the four owns, and states the two projection boundaries rather than only the nouns - knowledge and rationale becoming an executable software contract by a governed projection, and a generic execution primitive being adapted by a software specific service. It says explicitly that current placement does not prove permanent ownership, and names the subsystems that sit here for bootstrap reasons with a mature home that may be elsewhere. It carries an authority matrix answering which product answers which question, and an anti drift clause: a subsystem moves toward the lowest layer whose semantics fully explain it, and neither reuse alone, nor structure alone, nor current location alone decides it. It identifies any conflict with an existing decision explicitly rather than reinterpreting one quietly. Closed by the record alone: no crate moves, no package is renamed, no dependency changes, no integration is implemented, and AGENTS.md is not touched, because the harness gains a routing line only when a concrete routing question needs it.

items.why: P10-PHANTOM-FLOOR replaced CheckIndex::Incompleteness with Shortfall_For, so a claim is downgraded only when an unread subject could have declared that name, not whenever any subject anywhere was unread. items.title: A temporary hazard in the agent contract has no expiry, and the routing the contract promises is only half asserted
items.why: P10-AGENT-HARNESS landed the guard for the agent contract and stopped two checks short of what it promised. The contract routes architecture questions to README.md and to tests/contract and rationale questions to docs/records, and only the second pair is asserted - so an edit that drops the first two rows leaves the gate green and the routing table half real. The larger gap is expiry. The hazards written into the contract include one that is deliberately temporary: the stale binary that strips ledger fields it does not know, which names P10-STALE-WRITER as the item that will close it. Nothing connects the sentence to the item. Deleted early, the warning disappears while the defect is still live; left behind, the contract carries a hazard that no longer exists and every session spends a step defending against nothing. OD-AGENT-001 admits a temporary hazard on the condition that it can be removed rather than accumulate, and that condition is currently a promise rather than a check.

The contract is asserted to name all four of the routing authorities it claims, not two. The board is read through the ledgers own document type rather than by a second parser over the same JSON, since two readers of one schema is how they come to disagree. Each new direction has a negative control over a fixture. Not closed by deleting the stale binary hazard, which is still true while P10-STALE-WRITER is open, and not closed by asserting the item is open without also asserting the sentence is there.

items.title: A projection that agrees with its own stamp is not thereby what the store renders
items.why: Check compares two things and not the third. It rebuilds the projection, compares the recorded inputs_digest and profile_digest against the rebuild, and compares the body on disk against the stamp own content_digest. It never compares the body against rebuilt.body, which Build has already produced and which is sitting in the same function. items.title: One crate chooses the platform, runs the verb and renders the answer, and a second adapter would duplicate all three
items.why:
The README plans transports around a headless core, with the CLI as one adapter and IPC, gRPC and MCP as others. nomos-cli is the only place any of them could be written from today. It is 4104 lines across six modules: spec.rs 1509, work.rs 1047, check.rs 827. work.rs imports FileLock, StdFileSystem, StdProcessLauncher and SystemClock from nomos-platform-std directly, so choosing a platform, running a verb and rendering its outcome are one body of code with no seam between them.

Naming a concrete provider here is not the defect. OD-RULES-001 makes nomos check a composition root deliberately, and a composition root is exactly the place permitted to name concrete things. The defect is that nothing separates composition from orchestration: a second adapter wanting the same work verbs would have to re-derive the claim, lease and finish sequence rather than call it, and the two copies would then drift with nothing able to notice.

This is cheapest to settle while there is one adapter and no second caller to migrate. It gets more expensive with every command added, and the board has more commands queued than it has adapters.
items.done_when: Where application orchestration lives is decided and recorded. Either a seam exists between choosing a platform, running a verb and rendering its outcome, such that a second adapter can call the middle one without taking the other two, and the work group is the case that demonstrates it. Or the record states why one crate holding all three is right for as long as there is one adapter, names what that costs, and says what would make it wrong. Not closed by moving code into modules inside nomos-cli: a module boundary no second crate can depend on is the same coupling at a different indentation.

items.title: Two authorities describe band 0 differently, and the wider one is the copy no test reads
items.why:
README line 36 calls nomos-contracts protocol truth that depends on serde and nothing else. Cargo.toml line 3 calls it the only authoritative statement of Nomos semantics. AGENTS.md says that when two authorities disagree the mechanical one wins and the disagreement is a defect worth an item. Here the mechanical one is also the narrow one, and the wide claim sits in a workspace manifest comment that nothing reads back.

What is actually missing is an admission rule rather than a phrase. Test_Contracts_Should_Depend_On_The_Allowlist_And_Nothing_Else constrains what band 0 may depend on, and Test_The_Readme_Should_List_Every_Member_At_Its_Declared_Band constrains where a member is listed. Nothing constrains what may be added to nomos-contracts, so the criterion is whatever the comment says, and every concept in the product can argue that it is a statement of Nomos semantics. The crate holds ten modules today and the argument for the eleventh is already written for it.

Nothing in the crate is wrong yet, which is the reason to settle it now rather than after a finding, an architecture delta or an agent type has been admitted on the strength of a sentence nobody chose.
items.done_when: One statement of what band 0 is for, in the authority that governs it, and no second wider statement anywhere else. The criterion says what earns admission rather than listing what has been admitted so far: crossing a subsystem, process or plugin boundary and needing one stable shared representation is the candidate, and the record says what a domain-local concept does instead. Not closed by deleting the Cargo.toml sentence and stating no criterion in its place, because an unstated rule admits everything the wide one did.

items.title: A profile can be pointed at one subject, so the same projection serves every subject rather than one
items.why: Every shipped profile projects the whole store into one fixed path. Profile.output is a String and Filter has no exact identity at all - identifier_prefix is the closest, and a prefix is not an identity, so FEAT-1 also selects FEAT-12, and on relations it only narrows the from end. That is why the four-formats-per-subject shape cannot be expressed today: generated/features/FEAT-123/design.md needs the same profile run once per subject, and the profile model has nowhere to put the subject. This is the mechanism the typed feature layer will stand on, and it is worth building before that layer exists precisely because it can be demonstrated on subjects the store already holds - the governing records - rather than on a schema nobody has agreed to yet.

Rendering the same profile for two subjects writes two outputs and neither contains the other subject content. An exact node identity is selectable rather than approximated by a prefix, and on relations it selects the edges at either end rather than only the ones the subject starts. The refusals are real and tested: a subject given to a profile that names none, a profile that names one run without a subject, and a subject that matches nothing, are three different messages and none of them is an empty file. items.title: Six normative requirements govern the work ledger, none is cited, and the blocker taxonomy drops one of their seven causes
items.why:
Volume 12 of the v14 corpus carries six normative requirements, WORK-LEDGER-001 through WORK-LEDGER-006, at authority canonical-normative-record and maturity accepted, in section volume-12.10-4-2-work-ledger-verification-and-decomposition. They govern the work ledger. Not one of the six identifiers appears in any tracked file in this repository: not in docs/records, not in work/ledger.json, not in source, not in a test. Measured by resolving all 363 requirement ids under 01_authoring/artifacts/requirements against every file git ls-files reports.

That alone would only say the corpus is large and this build is young. What makes it an item is that the ledger demonstrably descends from these requirements and diverges from four of them without anywhere to read why.

WORK-LEDGER-005 names seven typed blocker causes: dependency, decision, territory mismatch, external resource, needs-split, stale probe artifact, and other. Blocker in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/item.rs enumerates six of them, in that order, with matching semantics and near-matching wording. StaleProbeArtifact is the one that is absent, and the string "stale probe" appears nowhere in the tree. Six of seven in the corpus order is not convergent evolution; it is derivation with one variant dropped, and because no id is cited nobody can tell whether it was declined or overlooked.

WORK-LEDGER-001 lists thirteen things an item shall be addressable by. LedgerItem carries twelve of them - id, title, why, done_when, territory, state, depends_on, blocked, claim, verification, verified, and abandoned covering recorded completion evidence. The missing one is priority, and "priority" appears nowhere in nomos-ledger or nomos-cli. This board is worked by picking an item off a list that has no ordering, which is the cost, and it is currently paid without having been priced.

WORK-LEDGER-004 requires that verification recorded at completion time be distinguished from a later reverification sweep, and that a failed sweep create a visible regression record rather than erase the original evidence. LedgerItem::verified is a single Option<VerificationRecord>. There is no sweep, and a second write to that field would overwrite the first - the same class of loss OD-LEDGER-006 recorded for abandonment reasons and fixed there by making abandoned a list.

WORK-LEDGER-006 requires generated projections of the ledger by item, state, feature and testing status. Eighteen projection profiles exist and every one of them projects the specification store; none reads work/ledger.json.

WORK-LEDGER-002, four testing dimensions per feature with completion requiring each done or explicitly declined, has no counterpart in the schema at all. WORK-LEDGER-003, a predicate declared before work starts, is the one the tree already honours in substance, since finish keeps "no predicate at all" as its own answer.

P10-PACKAGE-SEAM is the precedent and the reason this is worth opening rather than noting. ARCH-001 and ARCH-002 were in exactly this position - corpus requirements about a subsystem this repository had already built - and D-132 puts the corpus above the plan. The answer there was two records that decided what the requirements bind and what they do not. This is the same question about the subsystem that has had more items spent on it than any other.
items.done_when:
Whether WORK-LEDGER-001 through WORK-LEDGER-006 bind this build is answered and recorded, in the shape OD-PACKAGE-001 and OD-PACKAGE-002 used for ARCH-001 and ARCH-002: each of the six accepted, deferred with what the deferral costs, or read as not reaching this build with the reason a corpus requirement does not bind the thing built to enforce it. Blanket answers are refused - the six differ, and 003 is already satisfied while 002 has no counterpart, so one verdict covering all six would be a verdict about none of them.

The record states, for WORK-LEDGER-005 specifically, whether StaleProbeArtifact is a declined variant or a missing one, because six of seven in corpus order is the strongest evidence in this item and it is the cheapest thing here to get wrong. Blocker gains that answer at the site the way D-134 put a universe mirror next to it, so the next reader of the enum does not have to re-derive the comparison.

Not closed by adding fields. Any schema change this decision calls for is a follow-on item with its own territory, because the exhaustive undeclared-key probe lives in tests/exclusion_holds.rs, which three open items already reserve. This item ends at a decision that names what would have to become true.

items.title: A run cannot report that a subject needs an agent, so the seventh reporting category CHK-003 requires has no state to be reported in
items.why:
CHK-001 through CHK-007 are normative requirements in volume 05 governing what a check run reports. CHK-003 is the one this item is about: every run shall report evaluated, excluded, unsupported, unavailable, failed, not-applicable, and agent-required combinations.

Applicability in crates/contracts/nomos-contracts/src/applicability.rs answers six of those seven and does it well. Supported, SupportedWithFallback and PartiallySupported are evaluated; ConfigurationDisabled is excluded; MissingCapability is unsupported; ProviderUnavailable and DependencyUnavailable are unavailable, split because the remedy differs; AnalysisFailed and Unparseable are failed, split for the same reason; NotApplicable is not-applicable and its doc comment already calls it the only positive statement about the absence of a judgment.

There is no agent-required. Ten variants, and none of them says a subject needs a model to judge it.

That absence is load-bearing rather than cosmetic, because the concept is already in the tree one layer away. EvidenceClass in the same crate carries AgentJudged, documented as the floor a claim arrives at when nothing corroborates it, and EvidenceClass::Is_Mechanical exists precisely so a model judgment cannot be reported as a check having passed. So the protocol knows the difference between mechanical and agent-produced evidence when it describes a claim, and has no way to say it when it describes coverage.

The consequence is that a subject requiring an agent has nowhere honest to go. It gets filed as MissingCapability, which says no installed provider offers the capability and points the reader at installing something, or it is left out of Coverage entirely. Coverage in crates/kernel/nomos-model/src/evidence.rs counts evaluated and excluded and lists gaps, and Coverage::Debt filters gaps to those that are coverage debt rather than deliberate absences. Agent-required is neither: it is work that can be done, by something that is not a provider. Both available answers are wrong in the direction this type exists to prevent.

The enum head comment says the type is deliberately exhaustive and that a consumer match should break when the protocol grows a state, because a new way for analysis to be incomplete is exactly the kind of change a consumer must not silently absorb. Agent-required is a way for analysis to be incomplete, and it is being absorbed silently today by having no variant at all.

Related but not the same question as P10-VACUITY-HOME, which is about where the no-vacuous-success guarantee lives. This is about whether the vocabulary can express the case at all.
items.done_when:
Whether CHK-003 binds this build is answered, and if it does, a run can say that a subject requires an agent without that being indistinguishable from a missing provider or from silence.

If the requirement is accepted, Applicability gains the state, Coverage gains whatever bucket keeps it out of both evaluated and Debt, and the record says which of the two current mis-filings each was, so the change reads as a correction rather than an addition. A test asserts that an agent-required subject is neither reported as evaluated nor counted as coverage debt.

If it is deferred or read as not binding, the record states that with the reason, and Applicability carries the answer at the site, so the next reader comparing the enum to CHK-003 finds the decision instead of repeating this audit.

Growing the enum breaks every exhaustive match on it by design. Those breaks are the item, not an obstacle to it, and any that fall outside this territory are named in the record rather than widened into it.

items.title: Three hundred and sixty-three requirements govern this build and fourteen are cited, so a requirement that is met and one that is not read identically
items.why:
The v14 corpus carries 363 requirements in 61 families under 01_authoring/artifacts/requirements, at authority canonical-normative-record. Resolving every one of those ids against every file git ls-files reports finds 14 named in a governing record, the ledger, or crate source. Of those 14, the ARCH and PKG cluster is deliberate, put there by P10-PACKAGE-SEAM; the rest are incidental mentions in the ingest pipeline.

The reflex reading is that the corpus is far ahead of the build, most of it governs phases nobody has started, and a low number is expected. That reading is wrong in the direction that matters, and measuring it is what produced this item.

Where the build has reached a requirement, it tracks it closely. EvidenceClass carries exactly EVID-001 eight classes, Authoritative through HumanAsserted, and EVID-001 also forbids collapsing them into one confidence number, which the type does not do. FactVariant carries exactly CAP-002 five variants. CAP-003 requires provider selection to compare guarantees and not merely availability, and selection.rs compares Guarantee on every axis and documents that it is deliberately not a score. Three requirements met, precisely, and not one of the three is cited anywhere.

Where it diverges, it diverges by one element and says nothing. Blocker carries six of WORK-LEDGER-005 seven typed causes in corpus order and drops StaleProbeArtifact. LedgerItem carries twelve of WORK-LEDGER-001 thirteen fields and drops priority. Applicability carries six of CHK-003 seven reporting categories and drops agent-required.

That is the finding. Met and unmet are the same shape from outside: an identifier that appears nowhere, next to code that may or may not honour it. The only way anyone has told the difference is by hand, three times in this repository so far, and each time it cost a full audit to establish something a machine could have reported. Three of the six comparisons above came out met, which means the hand audit is not merely expensive but mostly negative - the worst ratio a manual check can have.

This repository already refuses this exact class of ignorance everywhere else. tests/contract asserts the README tables against the workspace in both directions. OD-COMPLETENESS-001 records that a completeness guard is only as complete as its universe. D-134 makes a universe declare its own mirror. The one universe with no guard is the corpus that governs the whole product.

The machinery is also already here and pointed elsewhere: a traceability-matrix projection profile exists in nomos-spec-project, and like all eighteen profiles it projects the specification store rather than relating the store to the build.
items.done_when:
How a corpus requirement is related to this build is decided and recorded, such that a requirement which is met, one which is deliberately not met, and one which nobody has looked at are three distinguishable states rather than one.

The record names the bearer of the relation and why it is there rather than somewhere else - a citation at the implementation site, a registry the contract tests read, or a projection relating the store to the workspace - and states what it costs to keep honest, because a traceability surface that goes stale is worse than none. It says what happens to the 349 requirements nobody has assessed, since a scheme that requires all of them answered before any of them is answered will not be adopted.

Not closed by citing requirement ids in comments. A comment is not a universe and nothing reads it, which is the failure OD-COMPLETENESS-001 already recorded one scale down. Whether the answer is mechanically checked is itself part of the decision, and if it is not, the record says why the corpus is the one authority in this tree exempt from a guard.

Building the mechanism is a follow-on item. This one ends at a decision with a named first requirement family to carry it, and P10-LEDGER-CORPUS and P10-AGENT-REQUIRED are the two already open that would be its first two entries.

items.title: The gate is red because a committed record was never rendered, and the diagram it names is in nobody territory
items.why:
The gate is red on dev right now, at the Required projections step, and has been since 401b2d0.

That commit registered OD-GATE-004 and did not re-render diagrams/relations.mmd. The diagram last moved in c42f93b, one commit earlier, so the committed body is missing every OD-GATE-004 edge - eleven of them, since the record relates to seven others and seven relate back. `nomos spec freshness --into . --require diagram-set` is gate.yml step 51 and fails on exactly this.

Nobody did anything wrong in a way a rule would have caught. P10-RERENDER-HAZARD wrote the obligation into AGENTS.md in ea3c167, which is after 401b2d0, so the commit that broke it predates the sentence telling authors not to. That is the ordinary way a hazard gets documented, and it leaves one artifact already broken behind it.

Two more commits have landed records since, including 840ec47 for OD-TRACE-001, so the delta is now larger than the one commit that started it.

What keeps this from being a one-command fix somebody does in passing is that the command cannot be run correctly by most sessions, for two separate reasons.

The first is stated in AGENTS.md: the store is built from the files on disk, so rendering beside another session unlanded record bakes their work into the output, and the gate then fails on the commit that carries it. At the time this item was written OD-LEDGER-012 and OD-SYNTAX-002 were both on disk uncommitted under live claims, which is the normal condition of this tree rather than an unusual one. A correct render needs a moment when every registered record is committed, or an isolated checkout that has only the committed ones.

The second is territory, and it is the reason this is an item rather than a note. diagrams/relations.mmd is in no item territory. Every item that adds a governing record reserves its own record paths and not the diagram, so an agent that correctly re-renders after adding a record is writing outside its claim, and an agent that respects its claim leaves the gate red. OD-LEDGER-001 records that territory is declared rather than enforced, so nothing stops the write - which means the current state is that the honest agents are the ones who leave it broken.
items.done_when:
diagrams/relations.mmd matches what the store renders, and `nomos spec freshness --into . --require diagram-set` exits 0 against a tree whose registered records are all committed.

The render is taken from a tree with no uncommitted registered record in it, and the item says which commit it was taken at, so a reader can tell a correct render from one that happened to be taken at a quiet moment.

The recurrence is addressed rather than only the instance, because this will happen again on the next record and the obligation in AGENTS.md is prose that a machine does not read. Either the diagram is reserved by whichever item adds a record - which means saying so where item territories get authored, since the guidance to reserve both record paths is in the nomos-spec-change skill and does not mention the diagram - or something derives the obligation the way the gate lint step is derived rather than restated. Which one is the decision, and if the answer is that authors must remember, the record says why a repository that derives its gate step from gate.yml is content to leave this one to memory.

Not closed by re-rendering and saying nothing. That is the instance, and the instance is the cheap half.

items.title: Which substrate is canonical for a feature request is undecided, and the typed layer encodes the answer
items.why: The typed FeatureRequest/DesignSpec/FeatureResult layer cannot be started until this is recorded, because the schema is the answer written down: authored files with typed front matter and a derived store index is a different schema from a store that is the durable substrate with docs/records rendered out of it. OD-SPEC-006 decided the question for governing records and left the alternative priced rather than refused - stop seeding from include_str, seed from the bundle, make docs/records rendered outputs with a freshness check, and design a guard, because OD-SPEC-005 refused the obvious one. OD-SPEC-007 has since paid part of that price in general form: it established that what makes the guard a check is that side B is authored independently of the directory it is compared against rather than that it is hand-typed in one file, and built registration files that keep the independence while removing the shared edit. So the price OD-SPEC-006 quoted is out of date in the buyers favour and nothing has restated it. Deciding this per artifact rather than once is the second-authority failure this repository is organised against: feature requests in one substrate and records in another would put the split in the schema of every typed row.
items.done_when: A record under docs/records with its own registration under crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records decides which substrate is canonical for a feature request, on stated grounds rather than by preference, and restates the price of the alternative as OD-SPEC-007 left it rather than as OD-SPEC-006 quoted it. It says what the decision binds - the typed layer schema - and what it does not. Not closed by a record that says the question is open, and not by one that decides it for records again without saying what a feature request is.

items.title: A commit touching the ledger carries whatever other sessions wrote since the diff, and the message describes only its own item
items.why: work/ledger.json is one file and every session writes it, so git add work/ledger.json stages whatever other sessions added between the diff check and the commit. Nothing is corrupted and no territory rule is broken - territory governs who may write a path, and this is several sessions writing the same path legitimately - but commit messages systematically under-describe what they carry, and the history is the only place a reader can ask what a change was for. Verified twice inside five commits. 63d51ee asserts Nothing here is a code change; this commit is the transition, while its ledger diff adds P10-AGENT-REQUIRED and P10-CORPUS-TRACE, two items another session opened that the message never names. P10-CANONICITY-DECISION was itself introduced by bd724ee, whose subject is the P10-SYNTAX-V2 payload parser. 0b98305 is the counter-example proving this is avoidable rather than inherent: its subject is the opening of the item it carries.
items.done_when: A commit that changes work/ledger.json either describes the ledger transitions it carries, or cannot carry ones its author did not make. Which of those is the answer is the decision, recorded on stated grounds rather than settled by whichever is cheaper to write. If the answer is that authors must remember, the record says why a repository that derives its gate lint step from gate.yml rather than restating it is content to leave this one to memory - P10-DIAGRAM-OWED is being asked the same question about the diagram, and two answers that disagree must say why. Not closed by a hazard line in AGENTS.md unless the record exists and argues for exactly that. A mechanical answer - a verb that stages only the items its holder transitioned, or a check over the message - brings its own predicate and its own files, which means widening this territory before starting rather than during. The record is registered under crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records or it is not governing.

items.title: The requirement assessment registry OD-TRACE-001 decided has no home, so CHK-003 is Met only in prose
items.why: OD-TRACE-001 decided that an assessment of a corpus requirement is a declared entry committed to this repository and compared against the workspace by a test, never derived from the corpus at check time, because CI has no corpus and a check-time surface would be green by being unable to look. P10-AGENT-REQUIRED landed first and could not carry it. Its territory was two source files, two surface snapshots and one record, there is no work edit, and widening a territory mid-claim is the failure this repository has already had twice. So CHK-003 is assessed in the prose of OD-CONTRACTS-002 and in no machine-readable place, which is the state OD-TRACE-001 exists to end. Three requirements are already known to diverge or be met with nothing that can be read: CHK-003 (Met, by OD-CONTRACTS-002), WORK-LEDGER-005 and WORK-LEDGER-001 (both diverge by one element, per OD-TRACE-001s hand audit). Every day this stays open, a prose Met and an unexamined requirement keep reading identically, which is the exact defect OD-TRACE-001 measured.

A corpus comparison, if one is added, is corpus-gated and declared in corpus_gates.rs, and inherits the OD-GATE-001 hole visibly rather than hiding in it. Not closed by a doc comment citing a requirement id, which OD-TRACE-001 refused by name.

items.title: The substrate question is answered per artifact, and nothing records what decides it
items.why: The typed FeatureRequest/DesignSpec/FeatureResult layer needs a rule for which objects are authored as documents and which are born structured, and no such rule exists. OD-SPEC-006 answered the question for governing records on the evidence of the day and left the alternative priced rather than refused. P10-CANONICITY-DECISION reached the opposite answer for feature requests, and its own abandon reason names the hazard that blocks both: deciding per artifact would put two substrates in one build and encode the split in every typed row. That objection is fatal to a split drawn on artifact kind and says nothing at all about a split drawn on provenance, and the difference between those two axes has never been written down. Until it is, the next substrate decision is argued from preference, and ARC-SPECDB-001 says the specification is a database without saying which objects are born in it.
items.done_when: A record under docs/records with its own registration under crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records states what decides an objects canonical substrate, on the provenance axis rather than the artifact-kind axis, and says why the kind axis is refused rather than merely not chosen. The rule is stated so it applies to an object nobody has proposed yet. It carries the obligation in both directions: what a born-structured object owes in exchange for skipping the preservation machinery, and what an ingested document still owes. It names which existing decisions it extends and identifies any conflict explicitly rather than reinterpreting one quietly. Closed by the record alone: no schema changes, no crate moves, no profile is added, and diagrams/relations.mmd is not touched, because P10-DIAGRAM-OWED holds it.

items.title: The typed layer has no tables, and it cannot get them before a writer exists
items.why: OD-SPEC-008 leaves the physical layout open and hands it the constraint that only tables something writes to exist, because a table nothing writes to looks like a feature in a schema dump and is not one. That makes the layout and its first writer one landing rather than two: tables committed ahead of a writer would be that failure committed deliberately. This is the item that turns the two decisions above into a submission that persists, and it is the first thing to exercise the durable form P10-DURABLE-LOAD landed.
items.done_when: The layout OD-SPEC-011 decides lands together with the writer that fills it, so no table lands empty. A submission made through the surface OD-SPEC-009 decided is validated by the rules OD-SPEC-010 states, is persisted, survives bundle export and import as the committed durable form, and renders a projection carrying the freshness stamp ARC-SPECDB-002 charges it with. An incomplete submission is refused and stored nowhere. Public surface snapshots move for every crate whose API moves, and README names any crate this adds.

Declined.reason:
Superseded by P10-SUBMISSION-LAYOUT, which is this item with the territory the reading found. The defect is unchanged and still open; what could not be executed was this item, in three places, each measured against the tree rather than suspected.

The record identifier was consumed. This item reserved docs/records/OD-SPEC-011, and OD-SPEC-011 was published at 515fc26 by P10-VOCABULARY-REFUSAL for an unrelated decision, an unknown relation type refused by name rather than by a foreign key. Two items reserved one identifier, which is the failure the task skill warns about by name and which nothing checks. So this items done_when named a record that says something else, and its territory reserved the right to edit a committed governing record belonging to another decision while not reserving the file the work must write. The layout decision takes OD-SPEC-013; OD-SPEC-012 is spoken for by P10-EDGE-CONSTRAINTS.

The bundle could not be reached. crates/spec/nomos-spec-bundle/src/columns.rs enumerates every table and column by name, and export.rs carries a row guard returning BundleError::Incomplete when a table holds rows the exporter did not emit and a column guard returning UncoveredColumn for a schema column it does not carry. Any table this item adds therefore makes Export refuse until the bundle is extended. This item required the submission to survive export and import, and ran nomos-spec-bundle in its predicate, while reserving none of it.

The CLI module could not be registered. nomos-cli is a binary crate with no lib.rs, so a new request.rs is reachable only once main.rs declares and dispatches it, and main.rs was not reserved. The projection was out of reach for the same kind of reason: profiles are JSON compiled through the SHIPPED table in crates/spec/nomos-spec-project/src/catalogue.rs, and neither the profiles directory nor the catalogue was reserved.

Nothing was written to the tree under this item. P10-SUBMISSION-LAYOUT carries the same done_when plus the repair of the six citations in OD-SPEC-009 and OD-SPEC-010 that this collision left pointing at the wrong record, folded in rather than opened as a third item, because it is the same re-render.

One consequence is left behind deliberately rather than hidden: P10-EDGE-CONSTRAINTS depends on this item and is now stranded, because a declined dependency is still reported as DependencyUnmet, which Is_Retryable calls retryable. That is a dead end reported as a queue, it is the first time a declined item has had a dependent, and it has its own item.

items.title: A lifecycle edge may join any two nodes, because a relation type declares no domain, range or cardinality
items.why: OD-SPEC-010 rule 4 requires that `implements` resolve to an accepted design and `answers` to an accepted request, and states in its own text that it constrains the submission and cannot constrain the graph. Measured: relation_types carries name, tier and inverse_of and nothing else, nodes.kind is free text, and relations enforces only that both endpoints exist and the triple is unique. So an `implements` edge joining a suite to a table row is written without complaint, and the lifecycle OD-SPEC-008 describes is expressible and unenforceable at the same time. The constraint mechanism is what is missing, not the vocabulary: the seed table is five types and ADR-ARTIFACT-GRAPH-002's real vocabulary arrives with the corpus and supersedes it, so an item that invents edge names here would be inventing the thing the corpus already answers.
items.done_when: A relation type declares which node kinds it may join and how many of it a node may carry, declared independently rather than inferred from the edges already present. Writing an edge whose endpoint kinds the type does not admit is refused by name, and so is one that exceeds the declared cardinality; both refusals say which type, which endpoint and what would satisfy them. The five seed types declare their own constraints, and a type that declares none is refused at registration rather than defaulting to permissive. The new columns travel in the bundle and survive export and import, with a round-trip fixture covering them. OD-SPEC-012 records what a declared constraint is, why the seed vocabulary is constrained without being extended, and what happens to declarations when ADR-ARTIFACT-GRAPH-002's vocabulary lands. Public surface snapshots move for both crates whose API moves.

items.title: Which product owns a responsibility is a first-class question the contract does not route
items.why: ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 states what each of the four products owns and carries the authority matrix, and P10-ECOSYSTEM-BOUNDARY landed it precisely because that seam was held in conversation and in nobody file. The agent contract's authority table does not route to it. An agent asking whether a responsibility belongs to Nomos, KWB, XVPE or the repository's own tooling is sent to docs/records generically, which is the row for why a decision was made rather than for who owns a subsystem, and the specification-system scope drift this repository has already paid for is exactly the failure that question exists to prevent. The harness budget was sized for this: CONTRACT_LINE_BUDGET's own comment says the headroom is enough for a routing line to a record that does not exist yet, and the record now exists.
items.done_when: AGENTS.md routes the ownership question to ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 by naming its path, as a routing line and not a summary of what the record decides. The harness asserts the new route the way it asserts the other four, so dropping the row fails rather than passing quietly, and the path-existence check covers the record it names. AGENTS.md stays inside CONTRACT_LINE_BUDGET and carries no restatement of the ownership matrix -- the row says which question and which file, and nothing about the answer.

items.title: Every fact this build materializes is a leaf, so the dependency half of invalidation ships unexercised
items.why:
nomos-analysis carries a full transitive invalidation mechanism. MemoryFactStore keeps a dependents reverse index, Materialize takes a &[Dependency], Dependencies_Of reads them back, and InvalidationReport separates direct from dependent and prints "N through dependency edges". OD-ANALYSIS-001 took the snapshot out of a fact key so that reuse across generations would be possible at all.

Nothing that ships creates an edge. Every call site in the workspace passes an empty slice. crates/host/nomos-cli/src/check.rs:410 does, and says why - "No dependency edges: a syntax fact is a leaf, read from one file bytes and from nothing this store holds" - and crates/rules/nomos-rules/src/mirror.rs:861 does inside its own test harness. The only non-empty dependency array anywhere in the tree is crates/substrate/nomos-analysis/tests/fact_identity.rs:710, which is the crate exercising its own reverse index against a fact it invented for the purpose.

So InvalidationReport::dependent is a field no shipped run can make non-empty, and one fixture is the only thing standing between the transitive half of this store and dead code. That is the shape P10-FACT-BYPASS closed, one level in: the fact layer has a consumer now, and the half of it that makes incremental reuse worth having still has none. It is cheapest to settle while there is one capability, one registered provider and one rule. Every rule added before it is a rule written against a store whose interesting behaviour nothing has run.
items.done_when: A fact is materialized with a non-empty dependency edge by code that ships rather than by a test fixture, and a test drives the store transitive path rather than its direct one: invalidating the fact that was read reports the derived fact under dependent rather than direct, and Dependencies_Of returns the edge that was declared. What the derived fact is, is this item to decide and its record to state, including the alternative that the existing provider declares an edge over something it already reads, if that is honest, rather than a second capability invented to carry one. If no honest edge exists at this size, the record says so, says what dependent is therefore holding open, and names what the first real one will be and what will produce it. Not closed by widening the fixture: a test materializing its own dependency proves the index works and proves nothing about whether anything uses it. Public surface snapshots move for every crate whose API moves.

items.title: A superseded item can only be closed by hand-editing the board, so it stays Ready and is claimed again
items.why:
ItemState::Declined exists and no verb reaches it. crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/item.rs:147 declares Declined with its reason carried in the variant so an item cannot be declined reasonlessly, and Is_Finished at item.rs:167 counts it terminal beside Done. The verbs nomos work offers are list, show, add, claim, renew, takeover, finish, abandon, validate and audit (crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs:156-212). None of them produces Declined. abandon is the near miss and goes the other way: crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/exclusion.rs:215 states that the work was abandoned and the item returns to being claimable. So the only Declined item on the board, P3-RESTORE, holds a reason no verb wrote.

The cost is measured rather than hypothetical, on one subject. P10-REQUIRABLE-DECLARED is Ready right now and carries two abandonments, the second of which checked its clauses one by one against the tree and found three of four already landed by P10-REQUIRABLE-FLOOR and the fourth refused by name in the alternatives table of its own governing record OD-PROJECT-002. It is finished work that cannot be marked finished and wrong work that cannot be marked wrong, so it reads as available. One subject became three items - P10-REQUIRABLE-DECLARED, P10-REQUIRABLE-FLOOR which delivered the work, and P10-REQUIRABLE-SET which redid work already landed - and a session spent its run duplicating what was already committed. Abandoning does not help: it is what produced the two reasons nobody reads before claiming, because the state column says Ready and the reasons are behind work show.

Hand-editing is the only remedy today, and it is the remedy the contract forbids for the same class of reason OD-LEDGER-006 gives: shared coordination state edited outside the verbs loses the distinction between a state that was decided and a state that was typed.
items.done_when:
A verb moves an item to ItemState::Declined and requires the reason, so the state cannot be reached reasonlessly through the CLI any more than through the type. Who declined it and when survive the transition on the item, the way an abandonment does under OD-LEDGER-006, rather than existing only as prose inside the state. Whether declining requires holding the item, and what happens to a claim held when it is declined, are decided rather than left to whichever path the first caller takes. A declined item is refused by claim, is reported declined by work list, and is not something work audit answers for, in line with what P10-AUDIT-STATE settled about items nobody can act on. Refusals name the item and the remedy, per OD-LEDGER-014.

P10-REQUIRABLE-DECLARED is declined by the new verb, carrying the reason its second abandonment already recorded, so the verb lands with the subject that measured it rather than with a test alone.

A governing record OD-LEDGER-019 states what Declined means as distinct from Done and from an abandoned claim, why the reason belongs to the state rather than to the transition, and why abandon returning an item to Ready is correct and not the thing being replaced. The record is governing only once its file under crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records exists. README names the verb in the block it already lists the other ten in, and the public surface snapshot moves for nomos-ledger if its API moves.

items.title: A second fact producer arrived in a crate whose one determinism declaration is about the first
items.why:
P10-DEPENDENT-EDGE added nomos-lang-rust::rollup, which materializes nomos.cap.module.index from other facts. nomos-lang-rust already declares SyntaxFactProduction, and that declaration's own doc says what it is about: "Producing the nomos.cap.syntax.items fact for one file, by parsing it." The rollup is not that. It reads facts rather than a file, and its reproducibility argument is a different argument -- the member order is canonicalized by the provider rather than given by syn's walk, and its inputs are digests of other facts rather than bytes off disk.

Nothing is red, and that is the point worth stating. tests/contract/tests/determinism_declarations.rs quantifies per crate: Test_Every_Fact_Producing_Crate_Should_Declare_A_Strategy asks whether a crate that constructs facts has at least one declaration, and this crate has one. So a second producer can arrive in a declaring crate and be covered by a declaration that was never written about it, silently. That is the same shape as the defect OD-DETERMINISM-002 repaired one level up -- a producer predicate that cannot see a domain it does not look for -- and the guard cannot catch it because the guard's grain is the crate.

The declaration was not added under P10-DEPENDENT-EDGE on purpose. Test_Every_Declaration_Should_Be_Held_To_It_By_The_Harness requires every declared strategy to be registered in tests/integration/tests/determinism.rs, which was outside that item's territory, and a declaration nothing can falsify is worse than none -- that test's own message says so. So the honest move was to leave the rollup under the existing declaration and reserve the split. This item is that split, with the harness file in its territory this time.
items.done_when: Either the rollup declares its own Strategy and tests/integration/tests/determinism.rs holds it to the obligations its triple implies -- with the same axis-by-axis treatment SyntaxFactProduction gets, not a copied triple -- or SyntaxFactProduction is restated to cover both producers on stated grounds, in which case its doc comment says what the second producer's reproducibility rests on rather than leaving it to the reader to assume. If a declaration is added, it occupies a row of the contracts domain table and Test_Every_Declaration_Should_Occupy_A_Row_Of_The_Table passes without the table being widened to admit it. The public surface snapshot for nomos-lang-rust moves if a type is exported. Whether the per-crate grain of Test_Every_Fact_Producing_Crate_Should_Declare_A_Strategy is itself the defect is in scope to answer and out of scope to fix: if the answer is that the guard should count producers rather than crates, that is its own item and this one names it.

items.title: An autonomous work harness is being designed for this repository and no record says which of the four products owns it
items.why:
A design for an autonomous work harness proposes a goal model above the ledger, a model and effort router, a context builder, an execution supervisor, a run controller, a budget controller and a run history, placed as crates/autonomous/nomos-* and packaged as a Nomos product capability with agent runtimes as adapters underneath it. ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 already answers most of that question in the other direction, and it was written to stop exactly this placement being made by precedent rather than by decision.

Three of its clauses reach the proposal by name. Its description of what XVPE owns is "a task scheduler, a storage primitive, a process or window or telemetry substrate", which is the run controller, the run history and the execution supervisor almost word for word. Its fourth owner is repository and bootstrap tooling, which owns "the machinery that exists only to develop or preserve this repository", carrying the sentence that something written to get Nomos built is not thereby part of Nomos, and that assuming it is is how a scaffold becomes a shipped surface nobody chose to ship. And its anti-drift clause states that a subsystem moves toward the lowest layer or product whose semantics fully explain it, with "reuse alone does not make something XVPE" and "current repository location alone does not make something Nomos" written as rules meant to be cited.

One part of the proposal does have a Nomos claim, and the same record supplies it: Nomos owns change planning and the validation that execution satisfied it. A goal decomposed into a change plan, and a convergence check that the plan was satisfied, is that sentence. Routing a model, supervising a process and accounting for tokens is not, because none of those definitions mentions software.

So the harness is not one subsystem with one owner, and the cost of leaving that undecided is the cost ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 names for itself: work accumulated across an unstated seam has to be re-litigated when the seam is finally drawn. The proposal has already reached naming, and a crate called nomos-model-router is the placement made, not proposed.
items.done_when:
A record decides ownership per component rather than for the harness as a whole. For each of goal and plan, convergence validation, model and effort routing, context construction and handoff, execution supervision, budget accounting, and run history, it says which of the four owns it and why the semantics require that owner rather than which repository the code would be convenient in.

Or it decides that the whole harness is repository bootstrap tooling for now, states what that costs, and names what would make it a product surface - which is the shape ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 used for its own placeholders, and is a decision rather than a deferral.

Not closed by creating crates/autonomous/ and moving on: a directory is a placement, and the placement is the undecided thing this item exists for. Not closed by an entry in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md either - OD-AGENT-001 refused to write an undecided architecture into an instruction file, and ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 exists because of that refusal.

items.title: A predicate that stalls and one that is legitimately slow are the same TimedOut, so the only remedy is a bigger timeout
items.why:
Command carries one bound, timeout, at crates/platform/nomos-platform/src/launcher.rs:25, and ExitOutcome carries one non-verdict bucket for exceeding it, TimedOut, at launcher.rs:66. A benchmark honestly running for forty minutes, a test suite whose one hanging case has stopped the other four hundred, and a child blocked writing into a pipe nobody drains are the same value. The enum was built to keep "the check failed" apart from "nobody found out", which it does. It does not keep the reasons nobody found out apart, and those have different remedies: wait, kill the case, fix the reader.

The cost is recorded on this board rather than hypothetical. P10-LAUNCHER-PIPE met one of the three - a predicate that passes in 103 seconds by hand was recorded as TimedOut twice at 600 seconds because the launcher read no pipe until the child exited. The drain was fixed and the classification was not, so the next stall from a different cause presents identically, and the first remedy anybody reaches for is a larger timeout, which is the one remedy that is wrong for all three.

Unattended looping multiplies it. Nothing records that an argv has already stalled, so a controller that retries on a non-verdict re-runs the same hang for as long as its budget lasts, and each attempt costs the full wall bound before producing the same non-answer.
items.done_when:
A stall and a long run are different outcomes, and the difference is asserted by a test that drives both.

A command carries a wall bound and an idle bound separately, and observable progress resets the idle bound. The outcome distinguishes at minimum a child that produced nothing for the idle bound from a child that was still producing when the wall bound expired, and that distinction survives into what the ledger records for a predicate, so work show can say which happened rather than only that nobody found out.

Termination reaches the process tree rather than the direct child, because a cargo test killed without its test binary leaves alive the thing that was actually hanging. What was observed before the kill - elapsed time, last output, the argv - is reported rather than discarded, since the kill destroys the only evidence of why it was needed.

Not closed by raising a default timeout, and not closed by adding an Idle variant that nothing produces: the test driving a slow-but-progressing child and a silent child has to show two different values.

items.title: A session that runs out of context has no way to hand off, and the obvious fix would restate the contract in the handoff
items.why:
A session that exhausts its context has two places to put what it knows, and neither takes it. The ledger holds the claim, the territory and the predicate, which is what the next holder needs in order to start; it does not hold what this session learned and has not yet earned a record for - the hypothesis it ruled out, the command that hangs, the reading of a record that turned out to be wrong. The records hold decisions, and none of that is a decision yet.

So the state goes into a prose handoff, and the shape a handoff takes by default is a summary of the repository: the crate bands, the gate commands, the ledger verbs, the hazards. OD-AGENT-001 already refused that document once, for the reason that a summary of a checked file is an unchecked copy of it, and tests/contract/tests/agent_harness.rs keeps AGENTS.md honest about it. A handoff prompt is the same document at a different address, written by a machine at the moment it is least able to check what it is copying, and read by a successor with no way to tell the copy from the authority it was copied from.

The compression direction matters too, and it cuts the other way. Agent-to-agent text is worth compressing, but the qualifiers are the expensive part to lose. Unverified, failed, assumed, not run, and the provenance of a claim are exactly what a summary drops first and exactly what makes the successor either repeat the work or trust something nobody checked.
items.done_when:
The contract states what a handoff carries, and a test holds it to that.

It carries session-local state only: what was tried and rejected, what was observed and not yet recorded, and what the next action is. Everything reconstructible from an authority is a reference to that authority - the item id, the record id, the commit - and not a paraphrase of it.

Agent-to-agent prose is compressed, and the compression is directional. Identifiers, paths, errors, failures and the qualifiers that mark a claim unverified survive it, because the compressible part is the English and not the uncertainty.

agent_harness.rs asserts it the way it already asserts that AGENTS.md carries no band table: whatever states the handoff policy names no crate table, no gate command list and no second copy of the ledger verb reference, and every repository path it cites exists on disk. Where a decision is made about what a handoff must not restate, that decision is a record, because a policy about not duplicating authority cannot itself live only in the instruction file it is about.

Not closed by a skill: a skill is a procedure, and this is a constraint on content that a procedure would restate.

items.title: The module-index reader refuses an unknown record and ignores an unknown field, which is the same mistake at a finer grain
items.why:
nomos.module.index.v1's reader, added by P10-DEPENDENT-EDGE in crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust/src/rollup.rs, refuses a record tag it does not understand and says why: an unknown record is most likely a payload from a newer schema, which is precisely the case where guessing is worst, because the unknown record is where the missing information is. That argument is nomos-cap-syntax's and it is right.

The reader does not apply it to fields. Member_Record takes two fields off the iterator and Item_Record takes five, and neither asks whether anything followed. So `member\t<subject>\tread\t<something-v2-added>` decodes as a v1 member and the something is dropped, silently, by the same reader that would have refused a whole record for less. A consumer then acts on a payload it only partly understood while reporting a clean decode.

This is cheap to get right now and expensive later: the moment a v2 of this schema exists, every v1 reader in the wild is one that quietly discards the new field rather than one that refuses and names it. The refusal is what makes a schema version negotiable at all.

Not found by a test failing. Found by reading the reader against the doc comment directly above it, which is why the item exists rather than a fix having been slipped into the commit that introduced it -- rollup.rs was outside the territory of the item that noticed.
items.done_when: Parse_Index refuses a member or item record carrying more fields than the grammar defines, with a message naming the line and what was unexpected, in the shape the neighbouring refusals already use. The grammar comment on Encode_Index says that a record is exactly its fields and that a longer one is refused, so the rule is stated where the writer is documented rather than only where it is enforced. A test asserts both directions: a record with a trailing field is refused, and every record the encoder actually writes still round-trips -- the second is what stops the fix from being a stricter reader that refuses this provider's own output. Whether the same laxness exists in nomos-cap-syntax's Parse_Payload is worth measuring while here; if it does, it is that crate's item and this one names it rather than reaching into it.

items.title: The typed layer has no tables, and it cannot get them before a writer exists
items.why:
This is P10-REQUEST-LAYOUT with the territory the reading found. The defect it names is unchanged and is still the one OD-SPEC-008 left open: the physical layout is undecided, and it inherits the constraint that only tables something writes to exist, so the layout and its first writer are one landing rather than two.

What changed is that the item as authored could not be executed inside its own territory, in three places, each measured rather than suspected.

The record identifier was consumed. P10-REQUEST-LAYOUT reserved docs/records/OD-SPEC-011, and OD-SPEC-011 was published at 515fc26 by P10-VOCABULARY-REFUSAL for an unrelated decision, an unknown relation type being refused by name. Two items reserved one identifier, which is the failure the task skill warns about by name. The layout decision therefore takes OD-SPEC-013; OD-SPEC-012 is reserved by P10-EDGE-CONSTRAINTS.

That collision is already published, and repairing it is part of this item rather than a separate one, because it is the same re-render. OD-SPEC-009 cites OD-SPEC-011 as the layout record three times, at its What This Does Not Bind, Consequences and Status sections; OD-SPEC-010 cites it three more, including the binding clause that says it binds OD-SPEC-011 to a layout that can express an attributed sequence per field and a gap as a row. All six now resolve to the relation-type record, and spec/domain-specification.md has published them. A citation into canonical content that names the wrong decision is worse than an absent one, because a reader who follows it stops looking.

The bundle was not reserved and cannot be avoided. crates/spec/nomos-spec-bundle/src/columns.rs enumerates every table and column by name, and export.rs carries two completeness guards: a row guard returning BundleError::Incomplete when a table holds rows the exporter did not emit, and a column guard returning UncoveredColumn for a schema column the exporter does not carry. So any table this item adds makes Export refuse until the bundle is extended. P10-REQUEST-LAYOUT ran nomos-spec-bundle in its predicate and required the submission to survive export and import, while reserving none of it.

The CLI module could not be registered. nomos-cli is a binary crate with no lib.rs. A new request.rs is reachable only once main.rs declares and dispatches it, and main.rs was not reserved.

The projection was not reachable either. Profiles are JSON under crates/spec/nomos-spec-project/profiles, compiled in through the SHIPPED table in catalogue.rs, so rendering a submission needs a profile file and its catalogue entry. The surface snapshot for that crate carries SHIPPED as a signature and not as a list of names, so it does not move and is deliberately not reserved.
items.done_when:
The layout OD-SPEC-013 decides lands together with the writer that fills it, so no table lands empty. A submission made through the surface OD-SPEC-009 decided is validated by the rules OD-SPEC-010 states, is persisted, survives bundle export and import as the committed durable form, and renders a projection carrying the freshness stamp ARC-SPECDB-002 charges it with. An incomplete submission is refused and stored nowhere.

The layout satisfies what OD-SPEC-010 binds it to rather than merely coexisting with it: a field is an attributed sequence of values each carrying an origin of submitted, clarified, inferred or decided, where a later value supersedes an earlier one for reading and never replaces it in storage; and a decision gap is a row carrying its question, the fields it blocks and a severity, closable only by a citation. A refusal names every field that failed, the rule each failed and what would satisfy it, rather than the first.

OD-SPEC-009 and OD-SPEC-010 cite the record that actually decides the layout. Both are amended in place with their version bumped, and each says why the identifier moved, so a reader meeting the gap is told rather than left to infer that a citation rotted.

Public surface snapshots move for every crate whose API moves, README names any crate this adds, and both required projections are re-rendered from a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones the commit publishes.

items.title: A dependency that will never finish is reported as a queue, so an agent is told to wait for declined work
items.why:
Measured on the board as it stands. P10-REQUEST-LAYOUT is Declined. P10-EDGE-CONSTRAINTS depends on it, and nomos work list reports it waiting -- the word the listing uses for a retryable refusal whose own usage text reads a dependency is unfinished. The dependency is not unfinished. It is finished in the sense that nobody will ever do it, and no amount of waiting changes that.

The mechanism is one comparison. Contested_By in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/store.rs compares each dependency against Done and reports anything else as ClaimRefusal::DependencyUnmet, which Is_Retryable in exclusion.rs reports as retryable and Refusal_Label in crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs labels waiting. That is right while the dependency can still be finished and wrong the moment it is declined, and the two cases are indistinguishable to every caller.

AGENTS.md tells an agent to branch on exit codes because retryable and fatal are different codes for a reason. This is the ledger itself collapsing them, in the one place an agent is told to trust.

It has never fired before and that is why it survived. P3-RESTORE was the only declined item for the life of the board and nothing depended on it, so no declined item had ever had a dependent until now. OD-LEDGER-019 gave the board a verb that produces Declined, which turns a latent gap into one that fires whenever a superseded item has a dependent -- and the first one already does.

There is a second, smaller defect in the same path, visible in the same refusal. The state carried into DependencyUnmet is format!("{:?}", found.state), and ItemState::Declined carries its whole reason in the variant, so the refusal string for a declined dependency embeds the entire declination prose. A refusal meant to fit on one line becomes several paragraphs.

The remedy is not obvious and is the substance of this item rather than a detail of it. A declined dependency must not satisfy the edge, because that would let an item claim groundwork laid by work somebody decided not to do. It must not read as retryable either. What is left is a refusal that says the dependency will not happen and that the dependent needs re-pointing -- and there is no verb that re-points it, so this item has to say what a holder is supposed to do next rather than only what they cannot do.
items.done_when:
Claiming an item whose dependency is Declined is refused non-retryably, by its own arm rather than by DependencyUnmet, and the refusal names the dependent, the declined dependency and what the holder is to do next. Is_Retryable reports it false, and the listing gives it a word of its own rather than waiting, so a reader can tell a queue from a dead end without opening the JSON.

The refusal carries a bounded rendering of the dependency state rather than the Debug form of ItemState::Declined, so a declination reason does not become the body of a one-line refusal.

What a holder is to do next is decided rather than implied. A dependency edge pointing at declined work can only be corrected by closing and re-authoring the dependent today, and this item either states that as the answer with its cost admitted, or records what would replace it; whichever it decides, it says so where the refusal sends the reader.

P10-EDGE-CONSTRAINTS is the measured instance and is not left stranded: it is either re-pointed by whatever this item decides, or closed and re-authored against P10-SUBMISSION-LAYOUT, with the choice argued rather than taken by default.

A governing record OD-LEDGER-020 states what a declined dependency does to a dependent and why it neither satisfies nor merely blocks. It is governing only once its file under crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records exists. Public surface snapshots move for nomos-ledger if its API moves, and the required projections are re-rendered from a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones the commit publishes.

items.title: A record identifier that is already published can be reserved again, because work add compares only against open items
items.why: P10-DERIVED-FACT reserves docs/records/OD-ANALYSIS-002 and its registration file. Both were published by 0bcaf6d under P10-DEPENDENT-EDGE, so the identifier is spent while the item still holds it. P10-REQUEST-LAYOUT reserves docs/records/OD-SPEC-011, published by 515fc26 under P10-VOCABULARY-REFUSAL. Two open items now reserve identifiers naming records already on disk. work add refuses a duplicate item id and nothing else: P10-ADD-PROMISE closed by narrowing the doc comment rather than adding the territory check, so the only guard is that an author remembers to look. Nothing reddens today because a spent identifier excludes nobody. The collision that reddens Test_A_Record_Should_Exclude_Nobody_But_Its_Own_Writer is two OPEN items on one identifier, not one open item on a published one, which is exactly why nothing will catch this. Whoever claims either item finds the identifier taken mid-claim, and there is no work edit to move it.
items.done_when: work add refuses a territory naming a record identifier that already resolves to a file under docs/records, and names that file in the refusal. It exits as a usage refusal rather than a store error, because the author fixes it by choosing another identifier. A test asserts the refusal, and its negative control is that an unspent identifier is still accepted. The two items already carrying spent identifiers are named and each is either retired or reissued, rather than left as the first thing the new check would have caught. Not closed by a doc comment telling authors to check, which is what P10-ADD-PROMISE already did.

Declined.reason:
Superseded by P11-SPENT-IDENTIFIER, which is this item with a record identifier of its own. The defect is unchanged and still open; what could not be executed was this item, and the reason it could not is this item's own subject arriving one step earlier than the item describes it.

Three open items reserved one identifier. This item, P10-DECLINED-DEPENDENCY and P11-SELECTION-AUTHORITY all reserved docs/records/OD-LEDGER-020 and crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/OD-LEDGER-020.record, authored by three sessions each reaching for the next free OD-LEDGER number. work add refuses a duplicate item id and nothing else, so nothing compared them. That is the missing check this item names, against an identifier that is unspent rather than published, which is why this item could not catch itself.

The collision was not latent, unlike the published-identifier case this item was written about. Test_A_Record_Should_Exclude_Nobody_But_Its_Own_Writer claims every open record writer on its records-only projection, and two open items on one identifier refuse each other there. It was red against the repository's own board, naming this item as the holder that refused P11-SELECTION-AUTHORITY, and it reddened every predicate naming -p nomos-ledger, including this item's own.

Three subjects, three records, rather than one record three items amend. OD-LEDGER-016 makes an identifier and the file it names one subject, so a shared reservation is the amendment case and it excludes correctly; the guard is right under either design and does not decide between them. What decides is that a declined dependency's effect on its dependent, what work add refuses at authoring time, and where the choice of next work is decided are three decisions and not three sections of one. P10-DECLINED-DEPENDENCY keeps OD-LEDGER-020 because its done_when names that identifier in prose. This subject takes OD-LEDGER-022, and P11-SELECTION-AUTHORITY's takes OD-LEDGER-023.

The two instances this item measured have both closed by other routes since it was written. P10-DERIVED-FACT and P10-REQUEST-LAYOUT are Declined, so no open item holds a spent identifier today. P11-SPENT-IDENTIFIER carries them forward as measurement rather than as an open obligation, and says so.
