items.title: The seam record governs knowledge becoming a rule and says nothing about a run's observations becoming knowledge
items.why:
ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 draws two crossings and governs both. KWB semantic intent projects down into a Nomos executable contract, and the projection is where authority changes hands, which is why it must be a recorded step rather than an inference somebody made once. XVPE generic primitives are consumed upward by adaptation rather than by extension. Neither of those is the crossing an autonomous run produces.

A harness that records what it did - task class, model, attempts, verification outcome, review findings, cost, failure cause - is producing observations about a codebase, which is Nomos's own subject matter and crosses nothing. What crosses is the step after it: generalizing many runs into a lesson that outlives the runs it came from. That is rationale and long-term epistemic memory, which is KWB's description in this record word for word, and the record has no arrow for reaching it from here.

The consequence is not that the step is forbidden. It is that it is ungoverned, and the specific risk is a loop the record's own governance step cannot see. Its last table row says a generalized lesson becomes an enforceable software rule only by a governed decision projected into Nomos, and that row is described as the one that does work. If runs write generalizations into KWB unreviewed, the review that later turns one into a rule is inspecting evidence produced by the machine the rule will govern, and the approval reads as independent while being circular. The downward arrow is guarded; the upward one is what would be feeding it.

OD-AGENT-001 recorded that the KWB boundary had not been decided by this repository, and ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 was the answer for the boundary it drew. This is the half that answer did not reach, and it becomes load bearing the moment a run is allowed to write anything durable about itself.
items.done_when:
ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 states whether observations produced by a run may become KWB knowledge.

If they may, it says what governs the crossing: at minimum whether a generalization carries the runs it was derived from as provenance rather than arriving as an assertion, and whether the review step that turns a lesson into an enforceable rule may accept evidence the system generated about itself or must have a second source. The record already treats the direction of a crossing as the interesting question rather than the boxes on either end, and this is a third direction beside the two it drew.

Or it decides the crossing does not exist yet, states what that costs, and names what would open it - the shape the record already uses for its own placeholders and the shape it says a placeholder should have.

Version 3 of ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001, not a new record. This is the crossing section of an existing decision, and a second record about the same seam is the duplication a seam record exists to prevent. Changing it leaves both required projections stale, so they are re-rendered from a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones the commit publishes.

items.title: An optional knowledge capability that is absent and one that found nothing would be the same answer
items.why:
A context builder is proposed that asks a knowledge capability for a bounded, provenance-backed packet - prior decisions, known failure patterns, previously rejected approaches - and that stays fully functional when no such capability is installed. ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 already permits the seam: the specification store's mature home "may be KWB, reached from here through a knowledge capability, which is already how the product is permitted to see it". So the open question is not whether the seam is allowed. It is what the seam returns when nobody answers.

The failure mode is one this repository has already met and fixed one layer down. OD-CONTRACTS-002 found that a subject needing a model "had nowhere honest to go", because Applicability answered six of the seven categories CHK-003 requires and folded the seventh into either evaluated or coverage debt. The remedy was a third disjoint bucket - Applicability::AgentRequired and Coverage::Agent_Required, neither Was_Evaluated nor Is_Coverage_Debt - with a test asserting disjointness over the whole enum rather than over a list of states somebody remembered. An optional knowledge capability has the identical shape. No relevant prior knowledge exists, and no capability was installed to look, are different facts with different remedies, and an empty packet reports them as the same one. Graceful degradation is exactly the mechanism that makes the conflation silent, because the run continues and looks complete.

Resolution has no answer for it either. OD-CAPABILITY-001 resolves a requirement with a floor and an optional preferred provider, and OD-CONTRACTS-002 states that the capability registry "answers about providers and only about providers", with WF-006 making executors a kind distinct from providers. A knowledge context provider is neither a mechanical provider nor an executor, so either the registry grows a third kind or the seam resolves somewhere else, and which of those is right is undecided.
items.done_when:
Either the resolution seam can say that no knowledge capability was installed, distinctly from a capability that answered and had nothing relevant, and a test asserts the two are different values rather than both being an empty result.

Or a record states where that distinction will live when a context builder exists, why the capability registry is or is not the place given that it answers about providers only and a knowledge provider is not one, and what a run reports in the meantime - which must not be silence, on the grounds OD-CONTRACTS-002 already established for the same shape one layer down.

Not closed by returning an empty packet with a flag beside it that nothing is required to read, and not closed by making the capability mandatory: the whole point of the seam is that the harness is complete without it, so the absence has to be reportable rather than eliminated.

items.title: Nothing computes what to work on next, so the choice is a model's and the board has already paid for it once
items.why:
Every ledger verb answers the same question. Claim, Renew, Release, Decline and Claim_Refusal all answer may I have this one, and none of them answers which one. The only thing shaped like selection is work list, and README says of it that the listing column is a snapshot and means nothing seconds later, which is a warning against using it for exactly this. So the choice of what to work on next is made by whichever model read the board, and two sessions reading the same board can differ with nothing recording that they did.

The cost is on this board with a receipt rather than being argued from first principles. P10-DECLINE-VERB's rationale records that one subject became three items - P10-REQUIRABLE-DECLARED, P10-REQUIRABLE-FLOOR which delivered the work, and P10-REQUIRABLE-SET which redid work already landed - and that a session spent its run duplicating what was already committed. The reasons that would have prevented it existed, as two abandonments on the item, and were behind work show while the state column said Ready. A selection step would have read them; a model scanning a listing did not.

This is not a defect in exclusion. Exclusion is what the ledger claims to do, it does it, and it refuses an unanswerable overlap rather than guessing, which is the property any scheduler above it would need and would otherwise have to reinvent. What has no home is the layer above: the eligible set, and the order over it.

It becomes load bearing rather than merely wasteful under unattended execution, because the same board read by the same policy has to yield the same choice before anything about a run is reproducible. A run whose first decision is unreproducible has no reproducible decisions after it.
items.done_when:
Where the choice of next work is decided is answered, and the answer is either implemented or recorded.

Either an eligible set is computed from the board rather than read off it - dependencies satisfied, not blocked, territory claimable now, refusals already known rather than discovered by attempting a claim - and the order over that set is stable, so the same board under the same policy yields the same choice, and a different choice is a change somebody made rather than a model that read differently. Ties break on something written down rather than on document order.

Or a record states that selection stays with the holder, says what that costs, names P10-REQUIRABLE as the measured instance rather than describing the risk in the abstract, and says what would change the decision.

If selection gains an authority, AGENTS.md stops instructing the agent to pick an item and names the thing that picks, and agent_harness.rs asserts that it does - because a contract file that still says pick is the instruction any session will actually follow.

Not closed by sorting the output of work list. Presentation is not selection, and a sorted snapshot is the same snapshot the README already warns about.

Declined.reason:
Superseded by P11-NEXT-WORK, which is this item with a record identifier of its own. The defect is unchanged and still open; nothing about the selection question was decided or given up here.

Three open items reserved docs/records/OD-LEDGER-020 and crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/OD-LEDGER-020.record: this one, P10-DECLINED-DEPENDENCY and P11-SPENT-RECORD-ID, each authored by a session reaching for the next free OD-LEDGER number. work add refuses a duplicate item id and nothing else, so nothing compared them. Test_A_Record_Should_Exclude_Nobody_But_Its_Own_Writer then went red against the repository's own board, naming this item as the one refused, and it reddened every predicate that names -p nomos-ledger.

One record per item rather than one record three items amend. OD-LEDGER-016 makes an identifier and the file it names one subject, so a shared reservation is the amendment case and it excludes correctly; the guard is right under either design and does not settle it. What settles it is that a declined dependency's effect on its dependent, what work add refuses at authoring time, and where the choice of next work is decided are three decisions and not three sections of one. P10-DECLINED-DEPENDENCY keeps OD-LEDGER-020, whose identifier its done_when names in prose. This subject takes OD-LEDGER-023.

There is an irony worth leaving on the record rather than deleting. This item is about the choice of what to work on next being a model's rather than something computed, and three sessions independently choosing the same next free record number is that choice going wrong in the smallest possible way. It is evidence for the item and it is not the item, which is why it is here and not folded into P11-NEXT-WORK's done_when.

Nothing was written to the tree under this item.

items.title: An item a person required and one an agent proposed are the same row, and neither says what kind of work it is
items.why:
The item schema is id, title, why, done_when, territory, state, depends_on, blocked, claim, verification, verified, abandoned, displaced and declined. Nothing on it says what kind of work the item is, and nothing says where it came from. work add refuses exactly one thing, an item that reserves nothing, and accepts everything else - any prose, any territory, from anybody.

That is a reasonable board for a person to write, and it becomes load bearing the moment work is proposed by the same thing that executes it. A design in progress for this repository has an agent observe something, propose work, and the system classify that proposal into a typed form before it is allowed into the graph. The classification step has nowhere to attach: there is no kind for it to classify into, and no origin field that distinguishes a proposal from a requirement. A proposed item and a required one are the same row, so the guard against a session inventing its own next subject would have to be a convention, and a convention is what OD-LEDGER-006 already records the ledger cannot enforce.

It also makes the board unreadable in the one direction that matters for ordering. State says where an item is; nothing says what it is. A validation obligation, an architectural decision, a correction and a cleanup are indistinguishable rows, so any priority over them has to be recovered from prose by whoever is reading, which is the same recovery P11-SELECTION-AUTHORITY is about not leaving to a model.
items.done_when:
An item says what kind of work it is and where it came from, or a record says why it should not.

If it does, the kinds are a closed set decided in the record rather than a free string, so an unrecognised value is refused by the same guard that already refuses an unknown field rather than being stored and ignored. Origin distinguishes at minimum work that was required from work a session proposed. Existing items are given kinds rather than left absent, because a field empty on a hundred rows and set on the next is a field nothing can be asked about - and the migration is the schema bump the guard exists for.

If a record says otherwise, it says what reads the board instead and how that reader recovers kind, given that any ordering over ready work has to be an ordering over something.

Not closed by a free-form tag list. This is a discriminant, and a list of strings is the prose it was supposed to replace.

Declined.reason:
Superseded by P11-ITEM-DISCRIMINANT, which is this item with a record identifier of its own. The defect is unchanged and still open; nothing about the item schema was decided or given up here.

Two open items reserved docs/records/OD-LEDGER-021 and crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/OD-LEDGER-021.record: this one and P11-ADD-NOT-DURABLE. work add refuses a duplicate item id and nothing else, so nothing compared them, and Test_A_Record_Should_Exclude_Nobody_But_Its_Own_Writer refuses two open items on one identifier, which reddened every predicate naming -p nomos-ledger.

One record per item rather than one record two items amend. OD-LEDGER-016 makes an identifier and the file it names one subject, so a shared reservation is the amendment case and it excludes correctly; the guard is right under either design and does not settle it. What settles it is that a discriminant on the item schema and a write that returned exit 0 and did not survive are two decisions and not two sections of one.

Which of the two moved was decided by the board rather than by authoring order. P11-ADD-NOT-DURABLE was claimed by claude-add-durable-b41 while this collision was being cleared, and decline refuses a held item retryably -- correctly, because ending an item is its holder's call. A held item is also the wrong one to move: its holder is writing against that identifier now, and taking it out from under them would turn one red guard into a mid-claim surprise. So the identifier stays where the live claim is, and this item, which was Ready and unclaimed, takes OD-LEDGER-024.

Nothing was written to the tree under this item.

items.title: A named re-export of another crate item is dropped from the surface snapshot rather than reported as unresolved
items.why: tests/integration/src/corpus.rs exports Subject_Of_Path by re-exporting nomos_model, and tests/integration/src/lib.rs re-exports it again. The crate still exports the name and slice.rs still calls it. The snapshot lost it: blessing nomos-integration-tests under P10-SUBJECT-HOME removed the Subject_Of_Path line from tests/contract/surface/nomos-integration-tests.txt while the export was still there, in commit a6f0e9c. OD-GATE-002 lists what the source-level derivation gives up and this is not on the list. It names the glob form, pub use module star, and promises that one is reported as an unresolved re-export rather than dropped. A named cross-crate re-export is dropped silently instead. The same record states, as a property explicitly NOT given up, that adding a name to a pub use list changes a committed file and fails the test until it is committed. For a target in another crate it does not. So the guard under-reports in a case its own record says it covers, which is worse than the documented false negatives, because a reader who checked the record was told otherwise.
items.done_when: A named re-export whose target is outside the crate is either resolved into the snapshot or recorded in it as an unresolved re-export, the way OD-GATE-002 already promises for the glob form. Silently dropping it is the one outcome ruled out. A test covers the case, with a negative control that a same-crate re-export still resolves. Superseded by P11-REEXPORT-GRAIN, which is this item with the territory the reading found. The defect is unchanged, the diagnosis in this item's why is confirmed exactly as written, and what could not be executed was the territory.

This item reserved one snapshot, tests/contract/surface/nomos-integration-tests.txt, because one dropped name had been measured. The mechanism is one comparison in tests/contract/src/surface.rs and it drops names in every crate at once, so the fix moves three snapshots and cannot move one.

Emit_Re_Export set a single resolved_any flag for a whole pub use declaration, so any name that failed to resolve was neither emitted nor reported whenever a sibling in the same list resolved. Reporting per name instead recovers fifteen dropped names in three crates:

  nomos-contract-tests      2  DeclaredUniverse and UniverseKind, re-exported from nomos_rules
  nomos-contracts          12  the identity newtypes, declared by macro_rules! expansion

The second and third are not this item's instance and are not separable from it either. tests/contract/surface/nomos-contract-tests.txt and tests/contract/surface/nomos-contracts.txt were not reserved, and the predicate cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests fails on both until they are committed, so the item could not have gone green inside its own territory.

The third is also a finding this item did not predict and the reissue carries. OD-GATE-002 lists macro-generated items among what the source-level reading gives up, and those twelve are exactly that -- but they are re-exported by name from the crate root, so per-name reporting makes twelve invisible exports visible as unresolved rather than leaving them absent. That is a wider claim than a glob's and it belongs in the record.

Nothing else was widened. Nothing reads Surface::unresolved outside surface.rs and public_surface.rs, checked across the workspace, so the blast radius is the three snapshots and the record.

abandoned.reason: Released so the item can be declined and re-authored as P11-REEXPORT-GRAIN with the territory the reading found. Nothing was left in the tree under this claim; the one edited file, tests/contract/src/surface.rs, is inside both territories and travels with the reissue.

items.title: An add that returned exit 0 was gone from the board minutes later, so exit 0 does not mean the write survived
items.why: Observed at unix 1786386100 in this tree. Two work add invocations ran back to back from one script against a freshly built schema-3 binary. Both printed their success line and both exited 0: added P11-SPENT-RECORD-ID reserving 6 paths, then added P11-REEXPORT-SURFACE reserving 5 paths. P11-SPENT-RECORD-ID is on the board. P11-REEXPORT-SURFACE was in no commit, git log -S over work/ledger.json finds it in none, and it was absent from the working tree minutes later. The window is locatable. Commit a2c0fed, written by another session while those adds ran, carries a work/ledger.json containing P11-SPENT-RECORD-ID and not P11-REEXPORT-SURFACE, so the file on disk had already lost the second add before that commit was taken. A writer therefore held a document read between the two adds and wrote it back after the second, dropping it. Which writer, and by what path, is NOT established: store.rs routes every mutation through With_Lock, which loads inside the lock, and finish.rs loads only to find the predicate and then goes through Release, so neither obviously has the window. That is what makes this worth an item rather than a fix. AGENTS.md and the claim verbs rest on exit 0 being the only thing that means the write happened, and OD-LEDGER-015 already records this exact failure once, for Claim, Renew and Release. This is a second instance reached by a different route, and the doc comment on With_Lock says in its own words that a description of an arrangement is what stops being true when the arrangement is bypassed.
items.done_when: The mechanism is established first and named in the record: which writer overwrote the file, whether it went through With_Lock, and if it did, how a load inside the lock still produced a document missing a committed write. Candidates to rule in or out are a second lock identity when a verb runs from a detached worktree with NOMOS_WORK_DIR set, a writer bypassing the single door, and a lock that is taken but not honoured across processes on this platform. Then the hole is closed so that a write which returned exit 0 is either present in every later read or the verb did not exit 0. A test reproduces concurrent writers losing an update and fails before the fix. Not closed by widening the lock wait, which changes the odds and not the property, and not closed by advice in AGENTS.md telling authors to re-read the board after adding, because the contract that exit 0 is the answer is the thing being repaired.

items.title: Engineering readiness and dispatchability are variants of one refusal, told apart only by a word the CLI prints
items.why:
ItemState carries Ready, Claimed, Blocked, Done and Declined. Whether an item can actually be worked on is not one of them: it is computed as a ClaimRefusal, and two of that enum's variants are turned into display words by the CLI at crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs:737-738, where DependencyUnmet becomes "waiting" and HeldBy becomes "held".

Those two words name categorically different facts. A dependency that is unfinished means the work is not ready to be done by anybody, which is a property of the plan and stays true no matter who is looking. A territory held by another session means the work is ready and somebody else is standing on it, which is a property of this second and is false again when a lease lapses. The ledger tells them apart correctly and tells them apart in a match arm that produces a string, so the distinction exists in the presentation and not in the model.

The consequence is that nothing above the ledger can ask the two questions separately. A caller wanting the work that ought to be done has to attempt a claim and read the refusal, or parse the CLI's words, and the one stored state that looks like the answer does not answer it: Ready means only not claimed, not done, not blocked and not declined. P10-REQUIRABLE-DECLARED sat Ready while carrying two abandonments explaining that its clauses had already landed, which is exactly how it read as available and was redone.

This is worth separating before a work graph exists rather than after. A design under discussion for this repository puts a scheduler above the board and leaves the board answering only whether a step can acquire what it needs right now, under a one-way invariant: coordination may withhold work that is otherwise ready, and may never make ready what the plan says is not. That invariant cannot be stated against a model where both answers are variants of one refusal, and it cannot be tested at all.
items.done_when:
The two questions are separable in the model rather than in the printing.

Whether work is ready to be done, and whether it can be started right now, are answerable independently by a caller above the ledger - without attempting a claim, and without reading prose. Refusals that mean the plan is not ready are distinguishable by type from refusals that mean the resource is busy, and the CLI's words are derived from that distinction rather than being the only place it exists.

The one-way invariant is asserted by a test: a condition that only affects dispatch can withhold work that is otherwise ready, and can never make ready work the plan says is not ready. The test states it over the whole refusal set rather than over the two variants somebody remembered, which is the shape OD-CONTRACTS-002 used for its disjointness assertion and the reason that assertion still holds after the enum grew.

Where the split is decided, it is recorded, because the decision is about which layer owns which question and that outlives the enum it is expressed in.

Not closed by renaming the display strings. Not closed by a derived boolean only the CLI consumes: the point is that something above the ledger can ask.

items.title: A record identifier that is already published can be reserved again, because work add compares only against open items
items.why:
This is P11-SPENT-RECORD-ID with a record identifier of its own. The defect it names is unchanged: work add refuses a duplicate item id and nothing else, so an author who reserves a record identifier somebody has already spent is told nothing, and the only guard is that they remember to look.

P10-ADD-PROMISE closed by narrowing the doc comment rather than adding the territory check, so the promise came out of the prose and the check never went in. Nothing reddens on a spent identifier because a spent identifier excludes nobody: the collision that reddens Test_A_Record_Should_Exclude_Nobody_But_Its_Own_Writer is two OPEN items on one identifier, not one open item on a published one, which is exactly why nothing will catch this. Whoever claims such an item finds the identifier taken mid-claim, and there is no work edit to move it.

The two instances P11-SPENT-RECORD-ID measured have since closed by other routes and are carried here as evidence rather than as work. P10-DERIVED-FACT reserved docs/records/OD-ANALYSIS-002 and its registration file, both published by 0bcaf6d under P10-DEPENDENT-EDGE. P10-REQUEST-LAYOUT reserved docs/records/OD-SPEC-011, published by 515fc26 under P10-VOCABULARY-REFUSAL. Both items are now Declined, so no open item carries a spent identifier today. The mechanism is untouched by that, and the next author reaches for the next free number the same way.

The unspent case is folded in here rather than opened as a third item, because it is the same comparison in the same function and a separate item would reserve the same file to make it. Three open items reserved docs/records/OD-LEDGER-020 and two reserved OD-LEDGER-021, each authored by a session taking the next free OD-LEDGER number, and that collision reddened Test_A_Record_Should_Exclude_Nobody_But_Its_Own_Writer against the repository's own board and every predicate naming -p nomos-ledger with it. So work add is silent on both halves of one question: an identifier a record already has, and an identifier another open item has already spoken for. The second half is what P10-ADD-PROMISE was opened for and decided not to build.
items.done_when:
work add refuses a territory naming a record identifier that already resolves to a file under docs/records, and names that file in the refusal. It exits as a usage refusal rather than a store error, because the author fixes it by choosing another identifier. A test asserts the refusal, and its negative control is that an unspent identifier is still accepted.

work add also refuses a record identifier another open item already reserves, and names that item. The two refusals are distinguishable rather than one message, because choosing a different identifier is the remedy for one and retiring the other item is the remedy for the other.

Both comparisons are decided by Territory::Intersect and Normalize_Path rather than by a containment rule written beside them. OD-LEDGER-016 already makes an identifier and the file it names one subject, and a second answer to that is what OD-LEDGER-005 records the cost of.

Only open items reserve. A Done or Declined item's territory is history rather than a reservation, in the sense Is_Open in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/tests/records_do_not_serialize.rs already gives that word, and refusing against it would make every closed item a permanent claim.

Not closed by a doc comment telling authors to check, which is what P10-ADD-PROMISE already did. No item on the board carries a spent identifier as this lands, so the check is proved by its own tests rather than by what it happens to catch on the day.

Declined.reason:
Superseded by P11-ADD-IDENTIFIER-GUARD, which is this item with a record identifier of its own. The defect is unchanged and still open. This is the second reissue of one subject, after P11-SPENT-RECORD-ID, and both were forced by the thing the subject is about.

P11-DISPATCH-SPLIT was added by another session reserving docs/records/OD-LEDGER-022 and its registration file, between the board read that chose OD-LEDGER-022 for this item and the add that took it. Both adds returned exit 0 and both are on the board; nothing compared them, because work add compares only item ids. Test_A_Record_Should_Exclude_Nobody_But_Its_Own_Writer went red again, this time naming this item as the one refused.

This item moves rather than P11-DISPATCH-SPLIT. It landed second -- index 121 against 122 in the ledger's own append order -- and it belongs to the session clearing this collision, so moving it disturbs nobody else's work. P11-DISPATCH-SPLIT is Ready and unclaimed and is deliberately left alone.

OD-LEDGER-025 is the identifier, checked against docs/records and against every open item's territory at the moment of authoring, which is the check this subject exists to stop being manual.

Nothing was written to the tree under this item.

items.title: Nothing computes what to work on next, so the choice is a model's and the board has already paid for it twice
items.why:
This is P11-SELECTION-AUTHORITY with a record identifier of its own. The defect it names is unchanged, and the reasoning below is the reasoning it was opened with.

Every ledger verb answers the same question. Claim, Renew, Release, Decline and Claim_Refusal all answer may I have this one, and none of them answers which one. The only thing shaped like selection is work list, and README says of it that the listing column is a snapshot and means nothing seconds later, which is a warning against using it for exactly this. So the choice of what to work on next is made by whichever model read the board, and two sessions reading the same board can differ with nothing recording that they did.

The cost is on this board with a receipt rather than being argued from first principles. P10-DECLINE-VERB's rationale records that one subject became three items -- P10-REQUIRABLE-DECLARED, P10-REQUIRABLE-FLOOR which delivered the work, and P10-REQUIRABLE-SET which redid work already landed -- and that a session spent its run duplicating what was already committed. The reasons that would have prevented it existed, as two abandonments on the item, and were behind work show while the state column said Ready. A selection step would have read them; a model scanning a listing did not.

There is now a second receipt, and it is the one that closed P11-SELECTION-AUTHORITY itself. Three sessions independently reserved docs/records/OD-LEDGER-020 and two reserved OD-LEDGER-021, each having read the board and chosen the next free number, and the ledger recorded five reservations without comparing any of them. That is smaller than the P10-REQUIRABLE waste and it is the same shape: a choice made from a snapshot by whoever was reading, with nothing above the ledger to make it once.

This is not a defect in exclusion. Exclusion is what the ledger claims to do, it does it, and it refuses an unanswerable overlap rather than guessing, which is the property any scheduler above it would need and would otherwise have to reinvent. What has no home is the layer above: the eligible set, and the order over it.

It becomes load bearing rather than merely wasteful under unattended execution, because the same board read by the same policy has to yield the same choice before anything about a run is reproducible. A run whose first decision is unreproducible has no reproducible decisions after it.
items.done_when:
Where the choice of next work is decided is answered, and the answer is either implemented or recorded.

Either an eligible set is computed from the board rather than read off it -- dependencies satisfied, not blocked, territory claimable now, refusals already known rather than discovered by attempting a claim -- and the order over that set is stable, so the same board under the same policy yields the same choice, and a different choice is a change somebody made rather than a model that read differently. Ties break on something written down rather than on document order.

Or a record states that selection stays with the holder, says what that costs, names P10-REQUIRABLE as the measured instance rather than describing the risk in the abstract, and says what would change the decision.

If selection gains an authority, AGENTS.md stops instructing the agent to pick an item and names the thing that picks, and agent_harness.rs asserts that it does -- because a contract file that still says pick is the instruction any session will actually follow.

Not closed by sorting the output of work list. Presentation is not selection, and a sorted snapshot is the same snapshot the README already warns about.

items.title: An item a person required and one an agent proposed are the same row, and neither says what kind of work it is
items.why:
This is P11-ITEM-KIND with a record identifier of its own. The defect it names is unchanged and the reasoning below is the reasoning it was opened with.

The item schema is id, title, why, done_when, territory, state, depends_on, blocked, claim, verification, verified, abandoned, displaced and declined. Nothing on it says what kind of work the item is, and nothing says where it came from. work add refuses exactly one thing, an item that reserves nothing, and accepts everything else -- any prose, any territory, from anybody.

That is a reasonable board for a person to write, and it becomes load bearing the moment work is proposed by the same thing that executes it. A design in progress for this repository has an agent observe something, propose work, and the system classify that proposal into a typed form before it is allowed into the graph. The classification step has nowhere to attach: there is no kind for it to classify into, and no origin field that distinguishes a proposal from a requirement. A proposed item and a required one are the same row, so the guard against a session inventing its own next subject would have to be a convention, and a convention is what OD-LEDGER-006 already records the ledger cannot enforce.

It also makes the board unreadable in the one direction that matters for ordering. State says where an item is; nothing says what it is. A validation obligation, an architectural decision, a correction and a cleanup are indistinguishable rows, so any priority over them has to be recovered from prose by whoever is reading, which is the same recovery P11-NEXT-WORK is about not leaving to a model.

The citation moved with the identifier. P11-ITEM-KIND cited P11-SELECTION-AUTHORITY, which was itself declined and reissued as P11-NEXT-WORK over the same record-identifier collision that closed this item; the subject and the argument are unchanged and only the id it points at is different.
items.done_when:
An item says what kind of work it is and where it came from, or a record says why it should not.

If it does, the kinds are a closed set decided in the record rather than a free string, so an unrecognised value is refused by the same guard that already refuses an unknown field rather than being stored and ignored. Origin distinguishes at minimum work that was required from work a session proposed. Existing items are given kinds rather than left absent, because a field empty on a hundred rows and set on the next is a field nothing can be asked about -- and the migration is the schema bump the guard exists for.

If a record says otherwise, it says what reads the board instead and how that reader recovers kind, given that any ordering over ready work has to be an ordering over something.

Not closed by a free-form tag list. This is a discriminant, and a list of strings is the prose it was supposed to replace.

items.title: The add verb reaches the board around the store's one locked door, and the door is where the fix has to be reached from
items.why: P11-ADD-NOT-DURABLE establishes the mechanism and closes it in the store: FileLedger::Add now decides and writes under one lock acquisition, and a test in nomos-ledger reproduces the lost update and fails without it. Two files the repair needs are outside that item's territory, and it has none to spare because there is no work edit. crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs holds the caller, which today is a Load, a push and a Save with nothing held in between - that call site is the defect, and while it stands the store's new door is unreached and work add still exits 0 over a write that did not survive. crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/lib.rs must re-export AddRefusal, which is pub in a private module and therefore unnameable by the caller that has to match on it. This is authored as a second item rather than by widening the first because territory is declared and not enforced (OD-LEDGER-001), so widening a claim mid-flight is the thing that makes a declaration worthless. The two territories are disjoint and both may be held at once, which is the arrangement the board exists to express.
items.done_when: work add routes through FileLedger::Add, so its read, its duplicate check and its write happen inside one lock acquisition. AddRefusal is re-exported from nomos-ledger so the caller can name what it matched. AlreadyPresent keeps exit code 4 and LedgerUnusable reports as a store error, so no refusal that used to be distinguishable becomes indistinguishable. No Load-then-Save pair remains in work.rs's mutating path. cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-ledger -p nomos-cli passes.

items.title: A named re-export of another crate item is dropped from the surface snapshot rather than reported as unresolved
items.why:
This is P11-REEXPORT-SURFACE with the territory the reading found. The defect it names is unchanged and its diagnosis was confirmed rather than revised.

tests/integration/src/corpus.rs exports Subject_Of_Path by re-exporting nomos_model, and tests/integration/src/lib.rs re-exports it again. The crate still exports the name and slice.rs still calls it. The snapshot lost it: blessing nomos-integration-tests under P10-SUBJECT-HOME removed the Subject_Of_Path line from tests/contract/surface/nomos-integration-tests.txt while the export was still there, in commit a6f0e9c.

OD-GATE-002 lists what the source-level derivation gives up and this is not on the list. It names the glob form, pub use module star, and promises that one is reported as an unresolved re-export rather than dropped. A named cross-crate re-export is dropped silently instead. The same record states, as a property explicitly NOT given up, that adding a name to a pub use list changes a committed file and fails the test until it is committed. For a target in another crate it does not. So the guard under-reports in a case its own record says it covers, which is worse than the documented false negatives, because a reader who checked the record was told otherwise.

The mechanism is now located and it is one flag. Emit_Re_Export in tests/contract/src/surface.rs sets resolved_any once for a whole pub use declaration, so the report is per declaration while the resolution is per name. A glob was only ever reported because it is the sole name in its declaration; the promise held by accident and fails the moment a name that resolves stands beside one that does not.

That makes the defect wider than the one instance this item was opened for, measured in a detached worktree at HEAD with only the repaired reader applied. Fifteen names in three crates are dropped today: Subject_Of_Path in nomos-integration-tests, DeclaredUniverse and UniverseKind in nomos-contract-tests -- re-exported by name from nomos_rules, the same shape -- and twelve identity newtypes in nomos-contracts, declared by macro_rules! expansion and re-exported by name from the crate root. The last group is a case OD-GATE-002 does list as given up, and the difference is that per-name reporting makes those twelve visible as unresolved rather than absent, which is a stronger position than the record currently describes.

Three snapshots move for one comparison, which is why this item carries three and P11-REEXPORT-SURFACE carried one.
items.done_when:
A named re-export whose target is outside the crate is either resolved into the snapshot or recorded in it as an unresolved re-export, the way OD-GATE-002 already promises for the glob form. Silently dropping it is the one outcome ruled out.

The report is per name rather than per declaration, because a name dropped beside names that resolve is where a dropped one hides best. A grouped list is split across as many lines as it has unresolvable names, rather than reported whole, which would say that every name in the list is outside this crate when one is.

tests/contract/surface/nomos-integration-tests.txt regains the name it lost. tests/contract/surface/nomos-contract-tests.txt and tests/contract/surface/nomos-contracts.txt gain the fourteen the same comparison was dropping from them, in the commit that repairs the comparison rather than in a later one that would read as an unexplained widening.

A test covers the case, with a negative control that a same-crate re-export still resolves. The control matters more than usual here: a reader that reported every name as unresolved would satisfy the first clause and destroy the check.

OD-GATE-002 goes to version 2. It records that resolution is per crate, so a named cross-crate re-export is reported rather than resolved, and it corrects the standing of its own claim about pub use lists -- which was false for cross-crate targets and is true once the report is per name. It also records that a macro-generated item re-exported by name is now visible as an unresolved re-export rather than absent, which is a narrowing of the macro entry in What This Gives Up rather than a new concession.

Registered under crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records or it is not governing, and both required projections are re-rendered from a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones the commit publishes.

items.title: A skill restates a step of the contract and nothing checks that the two still agree
items.why:
AGENTS.md step 2 says to read the board and pick an item, or add one. Section 3 of .claude/skills/nomos-task/SKILL.md says choose an item, or author one. That is one instruction living in two files, and P11-NEXT-WORK reserves the first and not the second - so the item that exists to stop the contract saying pick can satisfy its own done_when while the skill a session actually opens still says it. The territory was authored short, and territory cannot be widened by anyone including its author, so the gap is not something the holder can close.

The general defect is the one behind that instance. agent_harness.rs already runs its route checking over the skill root, so a path named inside a skill is checked to exist exactly as a path in the contract is, and a skill's declared name must match the directory it is found at. What nothing checks is agreement. A skill may restate a step of the contract in its own words, and when the contract's step changes, nothing notices that the copy did not. The test file is explicit about the limit of its own reach, calling what it asserts the half of correctness a machine can check.

This is OD-AGENT-001's failure at one remove. That record refused to let an instruction file restate authority, because a summary of a checked file is an unchecked copy of it, and the harness test exists to keep AGENTS.md honest about that. A procedure that restates a contract step is the same copy at an address the record did not reach. CLAUDE.md already states the rule that would govern it - a skill earns its place only when it encodes a reusable multi-step procedure that cannot be reduced to one command plus a pointer to an existing authority - and nothing asserts it.
items.done_when:
A skill and the contract cannot disagree about a step they share, and the disagreement is caught mechanically rather than by a reviewer noticing.

Either a skill stops restating a contract step and routes to it, so there is one copy and the question cannot arise. Or, where a procedure must carry the step in its own words to be usable, the skill names the contract section it adapts and the test fails when the two diverge - which is a different assertion from the one that already runs, because a route can point at a file that still exists while saying the opposite of what the file now says.

The specific instance closes with it: once P11-NEXT-WORK decides where the choice of next work is made, the nomos-task skill does not instruct a session to choose independently of whatever the contract then says.

Not closed by editing the skill once. The item is about the two staying in agreement after the next change, not about this sentence.

items.title: A named provider can only be preferred, so a caller whose policy is that provider is answered by another and told in a field
items.why:
Requirement carries preferred: Option<ProviderId> and one builder that sets it, Preferring. There is one strength of naming, so a caller can say which provider it would rather have and cannot say that it must have that one.

What happens when the preference is not honoured is decided and is not a defect. registry.rs:346-352 returns Satisfied with Applicability::SupportedWithFallback, and the comment there gives the reason: the judgment still stands, its provenance is not what was asked for, and a caller that cannot tell cannot record why. Refusing outright would deny a caller who would have accepted the fallback, which is the same mistake OD-CAPABILITY-001 avoided when it declined to let the registry decide how far down a caller spends.

The gap is on the requirement side rather than the answer side. A named provider can be a preference, and it can also be the whole point. A caller that names a provider because that provider is the policy - the strongest reader for a subject that matters, the one implementation whose output is admissible downstream - is served a different provider, told so in a field, and nothing makes it look. Applicability::SupportedWithFallback satisfies Was_Evaluated, so the run reports a judgment that was made by somebody other than the one required, and reports it as evaluated, which is true and is not what was asked.

That is the shape OD-CONTRACTS-002 corrected one enum along. A state that is honest about what happened is not sufficient when nothing obliges the caller to distinguish it, and the remedy there was not a better label but a bucket the predicates could not fold away.

The exposure grows rather than shrinks. OD-CAPABILITY-003 admits per-subject fallback, so within one run a capability may be answered by two providers under two addresses, and a caller that required one of them has more places to not notice, not fewer.
items.done_when:
A caller can state that a named provider is required rather than preferred, and a requirement that cannot be met by that provider is refused instead of answered by another.

The two strengths are distinguishable in the type rather than by a convention about reading Applicability afterwards: a required naming that cannot be honoured produces an Unsatisfied resolution naming what was required and what was available, and a preferred naming keeps the behaviour that exists today, unchanged and still reported as SupportedWithFallback.

A test drives both against the same registry and the same unavailable provider, and asserts they produce different resolutions - not merely different applicability on the same Satisfied.

Where the distinction is decided, it is recorded, including why refusing is right for the required case when OD-CAPABILITY-001 declined to let the registry refuse on the caller's behalf: the difference is that the caller said so.

Not closed by a boolean beside preferred that only some call sites pass. Not closed by documenting that callers should check Applicability, which is the convention this item exists because nothing enforces.

items.title: A record identifier allocated once and a published record reserved for amendment are the same act to add, and both are refused
items.why:
work add refuses a territory naming a record identifier that is already published: "A record identifier is allocated once; choose the next free one", exit 4. That is right for the defect it was built for. P11-SPENT-RECORD-ID recorded that add compared only against open items, so a published identifier could be reserved twice, and five collisions had to be cleared one record per item in df42f5e.

It is wrong for the other reason an item names a published record. Amending one is ordinary work here: ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 is at version 2, OD-CAPABILITY-001 at version 2, D-134 was amended in place rather than superseded because six of its seven decisions were untouched. An item that amends a record must reserve it, because the amendment edits that file and territory is how this board keeps two writers off one file.

The two acts are now indistinguishable to add, and it refuses both. Measured on 2026-08-10 against ARC-HARNESS-001: refused by identifier stem and refused again by the full published filename, so there is no spelling that gets an amendment through.

The board already carries the proof that the refused case is legitimate. P11-ECOSYSTEM-UPWARD reserves docs/records/ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 and its done_when is version 3 of that record. It was authored before the guard landed and cannot be authored today, so the guard forbids an item the board is currently holding.

The immediate cost is a clause that cannot be answered. ARC-HARNESS-001 owes an ownership row for handoff, which P11-HARNESS-SEAM's done_when required and the record does not carry, and no item can be opened to add it while add refuses to reserve the record it would edit.
items.done_when:
Reserving a published record for amendment is possible, and reserving an unallocated identifier twice is still refused.

add distinguishes the two rather than matching on the identifier alone. Whatever separates them is stated where an author can find it before being refused, and the refusal for the case that stays refused says which of the two it is, because "choose the next free one" is advice that is wrong for an amendment and the author who reads it will renumber a record that should not move.

A test drives both against one board: an item reserving a published record is accepted, and a second item reserving an identifier another open item already reserved is refused, and the two refusal paths are asserted separately rather than through one shared assertion that either could satisfy.

Not closed by removing the guard. P11-SPENT-RECORD-ID measured what its absence costs and five items were declined to clear it.

Not closed by telling authors to reserve the registration file instead: both spellings are refused today, and a rule that depends on which of two paths an author happened to write is the kind of convention this board does not enforce.

Declined.reason: Territory is short of the work. The guard is crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/store.rs:217 and its test is crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/tests/exclusion_holds.rs:2824; this item reserved crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs and crates/host/nomos-cli/tests, neither of which holds the check it exists to change. Superseded by P11-AMEND-TERRITORY, which is this item with the ledger paths added. The defect is unchanged and still open: work add refuses a published record identifier reserved for amendment, and both spellings were measured refused against ARC-HARNESS-001.

items.title: The invalidation report names what became stale in traversal order and cannot say which facts are mutually dependent
items.why:
MemoryFactStore::Invalidate walks dependency edges transitively and the walk is already correct in the ways that are easy to get wrong. A seen set guards re-entry, Invalidate_One is idempotent because it returns false once invalidated_at is set, and the traversal is deterministic because dependents is a BTreeMap of BTreeSet. A mutually dependent pair terminates and each fact is invalidated once. None of that is the defect.

The defect is what the report carries. InvalidationReport.dependent is filled in frontier.pop() order, which is LIFO over the traversal, so it is deterministic and it is not a dependency order. A caller holding that vector cannot rematerialize from it: for A depending on B depending on C, the order the caller receives depends on where the walk entered, and rematerializing in it recomputes a fact from inputs that are themselves still stale.

Worse, a fact reached through a cycle is indistinguishable in that vector from one reached through an acyclic edge. Both are a FactKey pushed to dependent. So a caller cannot tell the case where some valid order exists from the case where none does, and the second case is not an error - mutually recursive subjects are the ordinary shape once facts are computed from other facts.

Nothing has noticed because the workspace has one derived fact. OD-ANALYSIS-002 recorded that the dependent half of invalidation shipped unexercised because every capability was a leaf, and the module rollup that has since arrived is one edge deep. One edge has no order to get wrong and cannot form a cycle.

Broadening is not this. It is computed per key over seen from IncrementalGranularity and answers how much more had to be invalidated than the cause implied. Dependency structure answers how the invalidated facts depend on one another. They are orthogonal and must not share a representation.

Rematerialization is deliberately outside FactStore, whose trait is Current, Historical and Invalidate. This item does not bring it in. The store does not have to decide how mutually recursive facts are recomputed. It has to stop hiding that the mutual dependency exists.
items.done_when:
The invalidation report carries enough structure for a caller to derive a valid rematerialization order where one exists, and to identify the regions where none does.

The condensation is expressed as ordered groups rather than as a sorted key vector, so that a group is either a single fact or a set of mutually dependent facts, and the group order is a valid order over the condensation. The existing dependent field keeps the semantics it shipped with; this is added beside it rather than redefining it, because a caller reading dependent today is reading what became invalid and that answer is not wrong.

Three graphs are driven against a real store and asserted, not one:

A depends on B depends on C depends on D produces groups whose order lets a caller rematerialize D before C before B before A, and the assertion does not depend on the traversal order the store happened to use.

A cycle over four facts produces one group naming all four as mutually dependent, and no claim of a total order among them.

A mixed graph, where an acyclic chain enters and leaves a two-fact cycle, preserves both: the acyclic ordering around the cycle, and the mutual-dependency group inside it.

Broadening stays orthogonal. No cycle information is expressed through it and no granularity information is expressed through the groups.

Where the distinction is decided it is recorded, including why the store reports structure rather than ordering rematerialization itself, and what the later rematerialization orchestrator owes on top of it: that rematerializing according to this structure must produce the same current facts as clean recomputation. That predicate belongs to the orchestrator and is named here rather than asserted here, because nothing rematerializes yet.

Not closed by sorting dependent topologically, which silently changes a shipped field and still cannot represent a cycle. Not closed by returning an error when a cycle is found: a cycle is a shape of the graph and not a fault.

P11-AMEND-RESERVATION reserved only the CLI; P11-AMEND-TERRITORY added store.rs and was correct until ef1c93f moved AddRefusal into its own file. The territory here reserves the decision and the sentence, which are now two files, and the reissue reason on P11-AMEND-TERRITORY records that eight open items were left in the same state by that sweep.
items.done_when:
Reserving a published record for amendment is possible, and reserving an unallocated identifier twice is still refused.

The check in store.rs distinguishes the two rather than matching on the identifier alone. Whatever separates them is stated where an author meets it, and the refusal that remains says which of the two cases it is - because "choose the next free one" is advice that is wrong for an amendment, and an author who follows it renumbers a record that should not move. The wording lives in AddRefusal::Describe, so add_refusal.rs is reserved and the sentence changes with the check rather than a release later.

exclusion_holds.rs drives both against one board: an item reserving a published record is accepted, and a second item reserving an identifier another open item already reserves is refused. The two are asserted separately rather than through one shared assertion either could satisfy.

The ledger surface snapshot moves with whatever the distinction costs the public API, since tests/contract/surface/nomos-ledger.txt carries both AddRefusal and FileLedger::Add and the predicate names nomos-contract-tests.

Not closed by removing the guard - P11-SPENT-RECORD-ID measured what its absence cost, and five items were declined to clear it. Not closed by having authors reserve the registration file instead: both spellings are refused today, and a rule that turns on which of two paths an author happened to write is the kind of convention this board does not enforce. Not closed by a schema field on the item either, unless the amendment is worth keeping on the board after the item closes - a new ledger field is a stale-writer hazard on a file two sessions share, and OD-LEDGER-008 is the record that prices it.

items.title: The harness ownership table owes a handoff row, and a deferral of what a handoff may carry is standing in for it
items.why:
ARC-HARNESS-001 decides ownership per component and its table carries ten rows. Handoff is not one of them.

P11-HARNESS-SEAM's done_when named the components the record had to answer for by list: "goal and plan, convergence validation, model and effort routing, context construction and handoff, execution supervision, budget accounting, and run history". Nine of those ten words are rows in the table. Handoff is answered nowhere in it.

What the record says about handoff instead is one line under What This Record Does Not Decide: "What a handoff may carry belongs to P11-AGENT-CONTINUATION." That is a deferral of the mechanism, and it is correct as far as it goes. It is not the ownership decision, and it currently stands in for one - a reader looking for who owns handoff finds a sentence that answers a different question and stops looking, which is the failure mode the record was written to prevent for every other component.

The two are genuinely different questions here, which is why the substitution is not harmless. What a handoff may carry is a content question and its answer is bounded by OD-AGENT-001, because a handoff that restates the contract promotes an instruction file into the seam. Who owns handoff is the question this record answers for everything else: a handoff is state crossing a session boundary, and whether that is a generic continuation primitive or an engineering artifact about a codebase decides where it is built. The table's own two-owner rows exist for cases where the honest answer is both, and handoff may well be one.

It survived work finish for a reason worth keeping rather than fixing: the item's predicate is a test suite, and a test suite cannot read a done_when. Nothing mechanical compares a record's table against the list its item required, so the omission was invisible to everything except a reader who had both open.

It could not be repaired until now. work add refused to reserve a published record, so no item could be opened to edit the record it would edit; OD-LEDGER-026 is that decision and this is the first item authored through it.
items.done_when:
The ownership table carries a handoff row, naming an owner and the semantics that require that owner rather than the repository the code would be convenient in - the same standard the other ten rows meet, and the two-owner shape is available if the honest answer is both.

What This Record Does Not Decide no longer reads as though the mechanism deferral were the ownership answer. The P11-AGENT-CONTINUATION sentence stays, because deferring what a handoff may carry is still correct; what changes is that it stops being the only thing the record says about handoff.

The record goes to version 2, and the amendment is in place rather than superseding, on the same reasoning D-134 was amended: ten of the eleven rows are untouched and cited.

Both required projections are re-rendered from a tree holding exactly the registered records this commit publishes, per OD-GATE-005 - and re-rendered after the last word is written rather than before.

Not closed by adding a row that says the harness is bootstrap today. The record already says that about every component in its closing section, and a row repeating it would answer where handoff will be built with a fact about where nothing is built yet. Not closed by folding handoff into the context-construction row either: context is assembled for a step and a handoff crosses a session, and one row covering both is the conflation that makes a table stop being read.

items.title: A gate that does not run on the branch it protects, and a ban policy nothing has ever executed
items.why:
Two declarations in this repository claim mechanical enforcement and neither is executed. Both were measured at 4844c2b.

The gate does not run on the branch the work is on. .github/workflows/gate.yml triggers on pull_request and on push to main. Every commit lands on dev - 4844c2b, 33ed874, 3e0d0eb, f2934e6 and d25e8ce all did, and none of them ran the gate. Nothing reaches main except by a merge, so the workflow named gate covers the branch that receives finished work and not the branch that produces it. Earlier in this session the gate was red on dev at the Lint step, and the only reason anybody knew is that a session ran clippy by hand. P10-DIAGRAM-OWED measured the same shape once already at the Required projections step, and its why says the honest agents are the ones who leave it broken.

deny.toml has never been executed. It configures four classes - advisories, licenses, bans and sources - and no step in any workflow runs cargo deny. D-130 cites it as governing: "deny.toml bans the GPU, windowing and UI crates on the default feature set", and the file itself says of that ban "This ban is what makes the distinction hold mechanically rather than by intention". It holds by intention.

Running it for the first time, cargo-deny 0.20.2 against Cargo.lock at 4844c2b:

  advisories  ok
  sources     ok
  licenses    FAILED, 22 errors
  bans        FAILED, 19 errors

Neither failure is a supply-chain finding, and that is the point rather than a mitigation. licenses refuses all 22 workspace members because [workspace.package] license = "UNLICENSED" is not a valid SPDX expression and [licenses] private is unset, so every publish = false crate here is read as unlicensed third-party code. bans refuses 19 of them because wildcards = "deny" and a { path = ... } dependency carries no version, so every first-party edge is a wildcard and allow-wildcard-paths is unset. The GPU ban D-130 cites does pass - there is no wgpu, egui, winit, ash or naga in the tree - and it has passed unobserved since the file was written.

That is the shape worth recording. An unexecuted declaration is not merely unverified; it is untested as a declaration. Three of this file's four classes were misconfigured in ways nobody could see, because nothing ran them, and the one class configured correctly proves nothing about the other three.
items.done_when:
.github/workflows/gate.yml runs on pushes to the branch this repository's work lands on, so a commit that reddens the gate is reported by the gate rather than by whoever next runs it by hand.

A gate step executes cargo deny over all four classes and exits 0, which means deny.toml is repaired rather than the check narrowed: licenses stops reading 22 publish = false crates as unlicensed third-party code, and bans stops reading every first-party path dependency as a wildcard. Neither repair weakens what D-130 cites - the ban is still checked on the default feature set and still refuses wgpu, egui, winit, ash and naga, shown by measurement rather than asserted. Not closed by running the two classes that already pass and omitting the two that do not.

The new step is not named Lint and does not carry continue-on-error. work finish derives its lint argv by scanning this file for the step named Lint (nomos_ledger::Derive_Step), and Test_Only_One_Step_Should_Be_Named_Lint and Test_No_Step_In_The_Gate_Should_Excuse_Itself in crates/host/nomos-cli/tests/gate_step.rs both assert against this file rather than a fixture.

How cargo-deny arrives on the runner is decided rather than defaulted. This workflow trusts exactly one third-party action today, on a mutable tag, and a second one is a trust decision rather than a convenience.

OD-GATE-006 records the principle the two share and is registered under crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records, or it is not governing. Its scope is the general rule and not these two instances: rust-version = "1.85" is unexercised on a nightly-pinned toolchain, and every determinism claim in this workspace is checked on one operating system. Those are P11-MSRV-UNCHECKED and P11-PLATFORM-UNCHECKED, this item does not do them, and the record names them so a reader can tell a principle with open instances from one written to dress up a single fix.

Both required projections are re-rendered from a tree holding exactly the registered records this commit publishes, per OD-GATE-005.

items.title: The gate's -D warnings and the workspace lint table are two authorities for one severity policy
items.why:
Cargo.toml lines 111 to 133 declare the workspace lint policy, mirrored from XVPE. clippy::all and clippy::pedantic sit at warn with priority -1; float_cmp, unwrap_used, arithmetic_side_effects and indexing_slicing sit at deny. The severities are deliberate and the file says why: the four denials are there because a panic on the analysis path is a determinism defect rather than a bug, since a replay must reach the same panic at the same step.

.github/workflows/gate.yml then runs cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, which promotes every one of those warnings to an error. So the distinction the table draws between warn and deny is real on a contributor's machine and erased in CI, and the effective policy is spelled in two files that disagree. An author who reads Cargo.toml to learn what is enforced learns something false, and the stricter of the two authorities is the one that is not written down as policy.

This is the shape OD-LEDGER-003 refuses for the lint command itself. That record derives the gate's argv from the workflow rather than retyping it into a crate, because a copy is a second source of truth that goes stale the day the workflow changes and two guards for one rule is how they come to disagree. The severities the argv carries are the same rule and got the opposite treatment.

Which way it collapses is a real choice and it is not behaviour-preserving in either direction. Dropping -D warnings makes CI accept pedantic findings it rejects today. Moving the strictness into [workspace.lints] makes every local cargo check deny what only CI denies now, which changes every contributor's inner loop and changes work finish too, because the derived argv runs on the author's machine before the item is recorded done.
items.done_when:
One authority states the severity of every lint this workspace enforces, and the other place stops restating it.

Which of the two survives is the decision, recorded on stated grounds rather than settled by whichever is cheaper to write, and the record says what the choice costs the side that loses: either CI stops rejecting something it rejects today, or every local cargo check starts rejecting something it accepts today. A record that only says the duplication is gone has not answered this.

nomos_ledger::Derive_Step still yields a runnable argv from the step named Lint. It refuses any run: line containing a shell metacharacter, so the surviving line stays one bare command, and Test_The_Derived_Lint_Step_Should_Still_Be_Clippy asserts the derived argv is clippy over this workspace.

The workspace is measured under the collapsed policy before the item is finished rather than after. If the new arrangement reddens exactly what -D warnings was already failing, that is the same set and costs nothing; if it reddens more, the item says how many and where rather than discovering it on somebody else's claim.

Not closed by deleting -D warnings and saying the table now governs, unless a clippy run under the new arrangement is shown to reject what the old one rejected.

abandoned.reason: Territory cannot do the work. The only collapse satisfying done_when removes -D warnings from the Lint step, and two tests assert -D in the derived argv of the real workflow: crates/host/nomos-cli/tests/gate_step.rs Test_The_Derived_Lint_Step_Should_Still_Be_Clippy, and crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/tests/gate_covers_finish.rs Test_This_Repository_Gate_Should_Still_Yield_A_Lint_Step. Both are inside this item verification predicate, so the predicate cannot pass within the four reserved paths. README.md line 210 restates the same command and is a third authority. Needs re-adding with gate_step.rs, gate_covers_finish.rs and README.md reserved; README.md is held by P10-SUBMISSION-LAYOUT today.

items.title: rust-version says 1.85 and this workspace has not compiled on 1.85 since it grew let chains
items.why:
[workspace.package] rust-version = "1.85" at Cargo.toml:69 is a compatibility declaration and nothing exercises it. rust-toolchain.toml pins the channel to nightly - for rustfmt's unstable brace_style option, per its own comment - so every build here and every build in CI uses a compiler far newer than the floor being claimed.

The claim is already false, and by a mechanism that is invisible without a build. There are nine `&& let` chains in this workspace, including crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/gate.rs:121. Let chains stabilized in Rust 1.88 under edition 2024. So the declared floor cannot compile the code that declares it, and the only reason nobody has noticed is that no toolchain older than nightly has ever been pointed at this tree.

This is OD-GATE-006's principle in its compatibility form: a declaration of what this workspace is compatible with is incomplete until something compiles it in that configuration. Unlike deny.toml it is not merely unobserved, it is wrong, and it will go wrong again on the next stabilized feature somebody reaches for.
items.done_when:
rust-version states a floor the workspace actually compiles on, established by compiling it rather than by reading release notes.

A gate lane exercises that floor on every run, so the next feature that raises it is reported by CI rather than discovered by a downstream consumer. The lane overrides rust-toolchain.toml explicitly, since that file pins nightly and would otherwise silence the whole check - a lane reporting ok while running nightly is OD-GATE-001's defect in a new place.

What the lane runs is decided rather than defaulted. cargo check on the floor and cargo test on the floor are different claims, and the item says which one rust-version is making here.

Cites OD-GATE-006 rather than allocating a record, unless the choice of floor is a decision that record does not already make. Tracking stable, pinning a number and dropping the declaration are three different answers; the identifier reserved here is spent only if one of them needs arguing.

items.title: Every determinism claim in this workspace is checked on one operating system, and it is not the one it is written on
items.why:
.github/workflows/gate.yml runs one job on ubuntu-latest. This repository is developed on Windows - every measurement in this ledger carries an F:\repos\nomos path - so the two environments that matter are the one CI checks and the one nobody checks.

What is declared and unchecked is not incidental here. OD-DETERMINISM-001 and OD-DETERMINISM-002 govern a set of determinism declarations, and six crates carry a determinism.rs to make them: nomos-analysis, nomos-workspace, nomos-spec-bundle, nomos-spec-project, nomos-lang-rust and nomos-lang-rust-scan. A determinism claim says the same input yields the same output, and the inputs that vary between a Windows host and a Linux runner are exactly the ones such claims are usually wrong about - path separators, directory iteration order, filename case, and line endings, which .gitattributes already has an opinion about.

.gitattributes states the risk in as many words and defends against exactly one instance of it. Line endings are load-bearing because content hashes are computed over file bytes and the governing records are embedded with include_str!, so "the same commit would validate on one machine and not on another" - and the defence is `* text=auto eol=lf` plus one test that fails on a carriage return in an embedded record. That is a single mechanism against a whole class, and the class is stated by the repository itself.

That is OD-GATE-006's principle in its environmental form: a declaration is exercised in every environment necessary for the claim to hold, and a determinism claim's necessary environments are more than one.
items.done_when:
The gate runs on more than one operating system, and the second is chosen because a claim in this repository depends on it rather than because it was available.

What the non-Linux lane runs is decided rather than copied. Running the whole workspace twice doubles the gate's cost, and the steps that could differ by platform are not the same set as the steps that are expensive - a lane that reruns the paperwork steps is paying for nothing.

A red lane is a finding and gets its own item. This item's territory is the workflow; a determinism defect the lane exposes lives in the crate that declares the determinism, which this item does not reserve and must not widen into. Saying so here rather than discovering it mid-claim is what P11-AMEND-TERRITORY cost.

Not closed by adding a matrix whose extra legs are allowed to fail. Test_No_Step_In_The_Gate_Should_Excuse_Itself refuses continue-on-error by name, and a lane nobody has to fix is the corpus-gate shape without the corpus gate's reason for it.
