items.title: A verification record says when it ran and never what it ran against, so still-verified and verified-against-something-else read the same
items.why:
OD-ANALYSIS-001 decides what identifies a fact, and the reasoning is that a key carrying the wrong thing defeats the reuse the key exists for. Nothing in this repository decides what identifies run evidence.

VerificationRecord in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/verification_record.rs carries argv, exit_code, output_tail, verified_at and gate. There is no revision, no tree digest and no reference to the territory the item reserved. So the ledger records that a predicate exited 0 at a wall-clock instant, and every reader has to supply the missing half themselves.

The consequence is not hypothetical and this board has it today. An item finished at unix N against a tree, then the tree moves under it -- a peer lands a module split, a record is amended, the item's own files are edited by the next item that reserves them -- and work show reports exactly what it reported before. 'Verified' and 'was verified once, against something else' are the same three words. That is OD-GATE-001's shape moved from a test that read nothing to a record that means nothing in particular: both report a pass while the thing the pass was about is absent.

It is also the gap under the gate half. Since OD-LEDGER-003 the record carries the gate's own outcome, because 'this item was verified' is only true of a tree the gate also accepted. That reasoning is exactly right and it stops one step short: a tree is what both halves are about, and neither half names one.

The precedent for how to add it is in the same struct. gate is Option<GateOutcome> with serde default, None on every record written before the gate was part of finishing, and the doc comment says that is a fact about those records and is left visible rather than backfilled. A revision field is the same shape and should be the same shape deliberately.

HAZARD, and it is the reason this item is larger than its diff. VerificationRecord is serde deny_unknown_fields, so a binary built before the new field refuses to read a ledger containing it -- that refusal is P10-STALE-WRITER working as designed. SCHEMA_VERSION at crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/store.rs:52 must rise from 3 to 4 in the same commit as the code, and every live session's copied binary starts refusing every work verb until it is rebuilt. ea3c167 did this accidentally and left dev unusable. Do it in one commit, and say so where sessions will read it.
items.done_when:
A verification record names what it was verified against, and work show can distinguish a record that still describes this tree from one that does not.

What identifies a tree is the decision, and it is not obvious. A git revision is cheap, is what CI and every reader already speaks, and is wrong in the one case that matters most here -- a dirty working tree, which is the normal state of this repository and the state most finishing happens in. A digest over the item's own territory is honest about what the predicate could have been affected by and says nothing about the rest of the workspace, which is where a peer's breakage comes from. A whole-tree digest is the strongest and the most expensive, and it changes on every untracked scratch file unless it is scoped.

The record says which, and says what the losing options give up rather than only what the winner buys. A record that only reports the field was added has not answered this.

Staleness is reported, not merely storable. A field nothing reads is a comment with a serializer: work show must say something different about a record whose revision no longer matches, and the item shows that output for both cases.

SCHEMA_VERSION rises to 4 in the same commit as the code that understands it, and the migration is stated where a session running an older copied binary will meet it -- the refusal already names the two versions.

Records written before the field are None and stay None. Backfilling a revision nobody measured would manufacture the exact claim this item exists to stop.

Not closed by storing the revision and leaving every existing caller printing the same sentence.

items.title: The report that decides what a run found never reads the enum whose first sentence is that unknown is not pass
items.why:
Applicability in crates/contracts/nomos-contracts/src/applicability.rs opens by calling itself the load-bearing expression of the product's first principle: unknown is not pass. A region no analyzer could read is not healthy, it is unknown, and the two must never render the same. Eleven variants carry that distinction and 189 occurrences across 30 files consume them - the registry, the analysis reader, the rules mirror, coverage and coverage_gap in the kernel.

crates/host/nomos-cli/src/check/report.rs contains the word zero times.

The report is not naive about the general problem, which is what makes the gap specific rather than an oversight. Its Examined struct carries two denominators deliberately, and its doc comment gives the reason: 0 findings over 400 files and 0 findings over 400 files none of which produced a fact are different claims, the second is a broken run, and the prototype reported the first shape for a check that had walked nothing. So the argument that a bare finding count is a lie has already been made here and acted on - and it stops one step short of the variant set that exists to finish it.

The consequence is that the surface a person reads can distinguish a clean tree from a broken walk and cannot distinguish a clean tree from an unexamined one. A subject whose provider is missing, whose toolchain is absent, whose parse failed or which needs a model contributes nothing to either denominator and produces no line, so it is reported by silence - which is exactly the rendering the enum's first sentence forbids.

It is worth doing now rather than with the next capability because every capability added from here makes the silence larger, and because the vocabulary needs no design work: the answer is to read a type that is already exhaustive, already has no Default, and already refuses to give a consumer a lenient arm.
items.done_when:
The check report carries applicability, so a run says what it could not judge and why, not only what it found and over how much.

A subject that produced no judgment appears in the report with its Applicability variant rather than by omission. Grouping is by whatever makes the answer readable at scale - per capability, per language, per variant - and the record says which, but a subject falling into MissingCapability, DependencyUnavailable, ProviderUnavailable, Unparseable, AnalysisFailed or AgentRequired must not be indistinguishable from a subject that was judged clean.

The run carries a roll-up verdict saying whether the claim is complete, and the exit code contract states what an incomplete claim exits with. This is the decision rather than the rendering: complete-and-clean and incomplete-and-nothing-found currently share an exit code, and whether they should stop sharing one is what the record settles.

Examined grows or is replaced. Two integer denominators cannot express eleven reasons, and adding a third integer is the shape this item exists to stop.

The negative control is the one that matters: a test in which a provider is absent must fail if the report renders that subject the same as a clean one.

The three overlap by construction: the same twenty-four-type file is one finding for its type count, one for its public surface breadth, and one for its length.

items.title: Nomos and a forthcoming KWB are co-designed on purpose, and D-122's accidental-convergence proof gate does not answer that
items.why: Nomos and a Rust rewrite of KnowledgeWorkbench are now being built with each other in mind, and D-122 only answers code that converges on shared needs by accident, not code designed for shared use from the start. Left unaddressed, that gap reads as license to either ignore D-122 for everything or to build the same substrate twice just to satisfy its proof. KWB itself is also no longer five incidental mentions; a new Rust repository is starting for it, and nothing records what that repository is or how it relates to the .NET one it replaces. ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 already has an open, unclaimed amendment item (P11-ECOSYSTEM-UPWARD) for a different seam, so this item adds D-135 and D-136 as standalone records relating to it rather than contending for the same territory.
items.done_when: D-135 states that generic code with no Nomos or KWB semantics defaults to XVPE the first time it is written, and that D-122 continues to govern only code that started product-specific. items.title: nomos-corrections: CorrectionCandidate, CorrectionPlan, and the deterministic stage-preview-commit-rollback door the domain table already prices
items.why: The determinism domain table in nomos-contracts (crates/contracts/nomos-contracts/src/determinism.rs line 38) already prices a Correction planning and staging row as StateTemporal / CrossRun / BitIdentical, and tests/contract/tests/determinism_declarations.rs records it UNOCCUPIED on purpose: nothing in this tree plans or stages a correction. nomos-rules judges and reports; the step that would apply a fix does not exist, so there is no domain to declare and a declaration would be a promise about code nobody has written. A repository-wide search confirms it: no nomos-corrections crate, no CorrectionCandidate, CorrectionPlan or ChangeSet type anywhere, and the word correction appears only in two doc comments describing future intent (nomos-contracts finding display_label, and nomos-model artifact_kind GeneratedOutput). The project's own planning document (advisory only, per D-132) puts this capability directly after gate semantics and states plainly: start deterministic, and do not add an agent executor until the mutation and validation contract is solid. The ledger already carries P11 items that build an agent-coordination harness for sessions working this repository; that is a different concern from an AgentExecutor that would apply a correction inside an end user's repository, and building the second before the first deterministic contract exists would be building on an unproven mutation path.
items.done_when: A nomos-corrections crate occupies the Correction planning and staging row of the domain table: it exposes CorrectionCandidate, CorrectionPlan and ChangeSet types and a deterministic preview, stage, validate, commit and rollback lifecycle over a workspace change, with no dependency on an agent executor or model backend. The UNOCCUPIED entry naming that row is removed from tests/contract/tests/determinism_declarations.rs, the crate's own tests pass, and its public surface is snapshotted at tests/contract/surface/nomos-corrections.txt.

Declined.reason: Territory short of the work, measured while holding the claim; full account in the abandonment reason on this item. Successor is P13-CORRECTIONS-2 with tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs and README.md added to territory.

Correction planning and staging row, which requires it to be a real cargo workspace member so
`-p nomos-corrections` in this item's own predicate resolves — Cargo.toml is reserved and
covers that step.

Measured against the tree at ce05196, holding the claim, nothing written. Adding the member
makes tests/contract's Workspace::Load() (crates/spec... tests/contract/src/workspace.rs:31,
running `cargo metadata`) see it, and two assertions in -p nomos-contract-tests then fail:
Test_Every_Member_Should_Declare_A_Band (tests/contract/tests/boundaries/graph.rs:155, needs

(tests/contract/tests/boundaries/readme.rs:77, needs a matching row in README.md's band
table). Neither bands.rs nor README.md is in this item's territory, and both are checked by
this item's own predicate, so the item cannot pass its own gate from inside its reservation.
The public-surface half is fine as authored: tests/contract/surface/nomos-corrections.txt is

User chose to log it as open intent rather than force a decision.

items.title: nomos-corrections: CorrectionCandidate, CorrectionPlan, and the deterministic stage-preview-commit-rollback door the domain table already prices
items.why: P13-CORRECTIONS carried this why and was declined only for territory, measured and recorded on that item: the determinism domain table in nomos-contracts already prices a Correction planning and staging row as StateTemporal/CrossRun/BitIdentical, and tests/contract/tests/determinism_declarations.rs records it UNOCCUPIED on purpose. No nomos-corrections crate, no CorrectionCandidate/CorrectionPlan/ChangeSet type exists anywhere in the tree. The project's own planning document sequences this directly after gate semantics and before any agent executor. This reissue adds the two files a new workspace member must also touch: tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs, which Test_Every_Member_Should_Declare_A_Band checks a new member against, and README.md, whose band table Test_The_Readme_Should_List_Every_Member_At_Its_Declared_Band compares to it -- both run inside this item's own predicate via -p nomos-contract-tests, so the item could not have passed its own gate without them.
items.done_when: A nomos-corrections crate occupies the Correction planning and staging row of the domain table: it exposes CorrectionCandidate, CorrectionPlan and ChangeSet types and a deterministic preview, stage, validate, commit and rollback lifecycle over a workspace change, with no dependency on an agent executor or model backend. The UNOCCUPIED entry naming that row is removed from tests/contract/tests/determinism_declarations.rs, the crate's own tests pass, its public surface is snapshotted at tests/contract/surface/nomos-corrections.txt, it is added to BANDS in tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs at a band consistent with its dependencies, and README.md's layout table lists it at the same band.

Declined.reason: Territory short of the work, one layer deeper than the first reissue. Full account in the abandonment reason on this item. Successor is P13-CORRECTIONS-3 with tests/integration/tests/determinism/{domains,declarations,harness,productions}.rs and tests/integration/Cargo.toml added to territory.

abandoned.reason: Territory short of the work again, one layer deeper than the first reissue caught. Occupying the domain table row requires Test_Every_Declaration_Should_Be_Held_To_It_By_The_Harness (tests/contract/tests/determinism_declarations.rs:97, run inside -p nomos-contract-tests, this item's own predicate) to find a matching Check::<Strategy> registration under tests/integration/tests/, scanned textually by Harnessed_Strategies (tests/contract/src/harnessed.rs:20). That registration has to actually compile and pass clippy -D warnings across the whole workspace, since work finish's derived Lint step (crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/gate.rs, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings) runs before the item predicate and is not scoped to this item's territory. Confirmed by reading the row's SCOPE (CrossRun): Cross_Environment_Owed maps CrossRun to CrossEnvironment::SecondProcess (tests/integration/src/verification/cross_environment.rs:29), not SecondProcessAndGolden, so no committed golden digest is needed (goldens.rs stays untouched) -- but a real production closure, a test in domains.rs, a match arm in harness.rs's Test_Name_For, an updated count and entry in declarations.rs's hand-maintained table (currently asserts exactly 7), and nomos-corrections added as a dependency of tests/integration/Cargo.toml are all still required and none of the five files are in this item's territory. Nothing was written to the tree under this claim; verified by reading only, holding it. Successor is P13-CORRECTIONS-3 with those five files added.

items.title: nomos-corrections: CorrectionCandidate, CorrectionPlan, and the deterministic stage-preview-commit-rollback door the domain table already prices
items.why: P13-CORRECTIONS and P13-CORRECTIONS-2 carried this why and were both declined only for territory, measured and recorded on those items. The determinism domain table in nomos-contracts already prices a Correction planning and staging row as StateTemporal/CrossRun/BitIdentical, and tests/contract/tests/determinism_declarations.rs records it UNOCCUPIED on purpose. This reissue adds two more layers the first two reissues found: the workspace-membership files (tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs, README.md) that P13-CORRECTIONS-2 added, plus the harness-registration files P13-CORRECTIONS-2 itself was missing -- Test_Every_Declaration_Should_Be_Held_To_It_By_The_Harness, which also runs inside -p nomos-contract-tests, requires a real Check::<Strategy> registration under tests/integration/tests/determinism/ that compiles clean under the workspace-wide Lint step work finish runs before any item predicate. The row's CrossRun scope needs a second-process comparison but no committed golden (Cross_Environment_Owed maps CrossRun to SecondProcess, not SecondProcessAndGolden), so goldens.rs stays out of territory deliberately.
items.done_when: A nomos-corrections crate occupies the Correction planning and staging row of the domain table: it exposes CorrectionCandidate, CorrectionPlan and ChangeSet types and a deterministic preview, stage, validate, commit and rollback lifecycle over a workspace change, with no dependency on an agent executor or model backend. The UNOCCUPIED entry naming that row is removed from tests/contract/tests/determinism_declarations.rs, the crate's own tests pass, its public surface is snapshotted at tests/contract/surface/nomos-corrections.txt, it is added to BANDS in tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs at a band consistent with its dependencies, README.md's layout table lists it at the same band, and it is registered with the integration harness: a Check::<Strategy> call in tests/integration/tests/determinism/domains.rs, a matching entry in declarations.rs's declared table and Test_Name_For in harness.rs, and nomos-corrections added as a dependency of tests/integration/Cargo.toml. cargo test -p nomos-integration-tests passes for the new registration, run directly even though it is outside this item's own predicate.
